item.content:encoded:
Are you a public health professional, epidemiologist, mathematical modeller, communications specialist, IT expert, finance professional, administrator, or another qualified professional seeking an international career in Europe? The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) offers career opportunities for professionals interested in strengthening Europe’s capacity to prevent, detect, assess, and respond to infectious disease threats.

Based in Stockholm, Sweden, ECDC is an agency of the European Union dedicated to protecting public health by supporting European countries in the prevention and control of infectious diseases. Its work involves scientific analysis, disease surveillance, outbreak preparedness, risk assessment, public health communication, training, and collaboration with national and international health institutions.

The Centre recruits professionals from a range of backgrounds and experience levels. Available positions may involve scientific, technical, administrative, operational, managerial, communications, financial, information technology, and other corporate functions.

About the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control

The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control is an EU agency established to strengthen Europe’s defences against infectious diseases. Its work contributes to the identification and assessment of emerging health threats and supports countries in developing effective public health responses.

ECDC’s activities may include:

  • Monitoring infectious disease developments.
  • Collecting and analysing public health data.
  • Assessing risks to European populations.
  • Supporting preparedness for disease outbreaks.
  • Providing scientific and technical guidance.
  • Strengthening disease surveillance systems.
  • Coordinating public health networks.
  • Supporting training and professional development.
  • Communicating information about infectious disease threats.
  • Working with European countries, international organisations, laboratories, and public health institutions.

According to ECDC, more than 400 people with different nationalities and professional backgrounds work at the Centre. The organisation brings together professionals such as public health experts, mathematical modellers, communication specialists, IT professionals, finance officers, and administrative support staff.

Career Opportunities at ECDC

ECDC’s staff positions are designed for individuals who want to contribute to public health protection in a multicultural and international working environment.

Depending on the vacancy, applicants may find opportunities in areas such as:

1. Public Health and Epidemiology

These positions may involve:

  • Infectious disease surveillance.
  • Epidemiological analysis.
  • Outbreak investigation and response.
  • Preparedness and response planning.
  • Public health threat assessment.
  • Disease prevention and control.
  • Scientific research and technical guidance.
  • Collaboration with national public health authorities.

2. Mathematical Modelling and Data Analysis

Professionals with expertise in mathematics, statistics, data science, modelling, or related fields may contribute to:

  • Modelling infectious disease transmission.
  • Analysing epidemiological trends.
  • Supporting forecasting and risk assessment.
  • Developing analytical tools.
  • Interpreting complex public health datasets.
  • Supporting evidence-based policy and decision-making.

3. Communications and Public Information

Communications-related roles may involve:

  • Developing public health communication materials.
  • Supporting media and stakeholder engagement.
  • Preparing reports, publications, and briefings.
  • Communicating scientific information to different audiences.
  • Supporting awareness and risk communication activities.
  • Managing digital communication and public information channels.

4. Information Technology and Digital Services

IT professionals may work in areas such as:

  • Digital systems and infrastructure.
  • Data management.
  • Cybersecurity and information security.
  • Software and technology support.
  • Enterprise systems.
  • Digital transformation.
  • Technical services for public health operations.

5. Finance, Administration, and Corporate Support

ECDC also recruits professionals who support the Centre’s internal operations. These roles may include:

  • Finance and budget management.
  • Procurement.
  • Human resources.
  • Administrative coordination.
  • Legal and compliance support.
  • Meeting and mission coordination.
  • Project management.
  • Organisational planning.
  • General corporate services.

The exact responsibilities and requirements depend on the specific vacancy published on ECDC’s recruitment platform.

Learn More HERE

Benefits of Working with ECDC

Working at ECDC provides an opportunity to contribute to public health protection while gaining experience in an international European institution.

Potential benefits of an ECDC career include:

International Work Environment

ECDC brings together staff members from different nationalities and professional backgrounds. Employees work with colleagues and stakeholders across Europe and may collaborate with national public health institutions, international organisations, laboratories, and scientific networks.

Contribution to Public Health

Employees contribute to work that supports the prevention and control of infectious diseases. Their activities may help strengthen disease surveillance, improve outbreak preparedness, assess health risks, and support evidence-based public health action.

Professional Development

ECDC offers opportunities to work in specialised scientific, technical, operational, and administrative fields. Depending on the role, employees may develop expertise in public health policy, epidemiology, data analysis, project management, communications, administration, or other professional areas.

Competitive Employment Conditions

ECDC states that it offers competitive pay and a range of staff benefits. Depending on the applicable employment conditions and individual circumstances, benefits may include:

  • Competitive salary.
  • Health insurance.
  • Learning and development opportunities.
  • Flexible working arrangements.
  • Teleworking options.
  • Flexible working hours.
  • Relocation support for eligible employees moving to Stockholm.
  • Applicable family or expatriation allowances.

Specific salary levels, allowances, and benefits depend on the position, contract type, staff category, and applicable EU employment regulations.

Opportunity to Relocate to Stockholm

Successful candidates may be expected to work in Stockholm, Sweden, where ECDC is headquartered. Applicants should therefore consider relocation requirements, residence arrangements, and the practical implications of working in another European country.

General Eligibility Requirements

Before applying for an ECDC staff position, candidates should review the general requirements listed by the organisation.

Nationality

Applicants must generally be nationals of one of the following:

  • A Member State of the European Union.
  • Norway.
  • Iceland.
  • Liechtenstein.

This means that applicants from countries outside the EU, Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein may not meet the general nationality requirement for ECDC staff positions, unless a particular vacancy specifies an applicable exception or different arrangement.

Language Requirements

Applicants are generally expected to:

  • Be fluent in English.
  • Have a satisfactory knowledge of a second official language of the European Union, to the extent necessary for the performance of their duties.

The language requirements may vary depending on the position. Candidates should carefully examine the language provisions in the individual vacancy notice before applying.

Age Requirement

ECDC states that applicants should be less than 65 years of age. The Centre also notes that it has a mandatory retirement age of 66.

Academic and Professional Qualifications

The required qualifications differ according to the position. A vacancy may require:

  • A university degree.
  • A diploma in a relevant field.
  • Post-secondary education.
  • A specific number of years of professional experience.
  • Technical or scientific expertise.
  • Experience in public health, administration, finance, IT, communications, or another relevant area.
  • Knowledge of specific systems, methods, or professional practices.

Applicants should not assume that meeting the general ECDC requirements automatically qualifies them for every vacancy. Each job announcement contains its own formal requirements and selection criteria.

For example, some ECDC vacancies require completed university studies of at least three years, while other positions may accept post-secondary or secondary education combined with relevant professional experience.

Diversity and Equal Opportunity

ECDC states that it values diversity and accepts applications without distinction based on factors such as:

  • Age.
  • Race.
  • Political, philosophical, or religious convictions.
  • Sex.
  • Sexual orientation.
  • Disability.
  • Marital status.
  • Family situation.
  • Ethnic or social origin.
  • Religion or belief.

The organisation encourages applications from suitably qualified candidates. Nevertheless, all applicants must satisfy the nationality, language, academic, professional, and other formal conditions stated in the relevant vacancy notice.

Application Deadline

There is no single application deadline for all ECDC jobs.

Each staff vacancy has its own application deadline. Applicants must therefore review the current vacancies listed on ECDC’s official recruitment platform and submit their applications before the deadline stated in the specific vacancy announcement.

Late applications are generally not accepted. Candidates are advised to apply well before the closing date to allow time for technical issues, heavy website traffic, or incomplete application information.

How to Apply for ECDC Jobs

Applications for ECDC staff positions must be submitted through the Organisation’s Official e-recruitment platform.

Step 1: Review Available Vacancies

Visit the ECDC vacancies and recruitment pages to identify positions that match your qualifications, professional experience, and career interests.

Read the complete vacancy notice carefully. Pay particular attention to:

  • Job title and reference number.
  • Main responsibilities.
  • Formal eligibility requirements.
  • Required academic qualifications.
  • Required professional experience.
  • Language requirements.
  • Nationality requirements.
  • Selection criteria.
  • Application deadline.
  • Supporting documents.
  • Contract type and employment conditions.

Step 2: Create or Log In to an E-Recruitment Account

Applicants must use the ECDC recruitment platform to submit an application. If they do not already have an account, they may need to create one before completing the application process.

Step 3: Complete the Application Form

The ECDC candidate guide indicates that applicants should complete all mandatory sections of the online application, which may include:

  • Personal and contact information.
  • Education history.
  • Professional experience.
  • Language skills.
  • Letter of motivation.
  • Eligibility declarations.
  • Declaration of honour.
  • Other information requested in the vacancy notice.

Applicants should provide accurate and consistent information. Dates relating to education and professional experience should be entered precisely because they may be checked against supporting documents during the selection process.

Step 4: Upload Supporting Documents

Depending on the vacancy, applicants may be required to provide documents such as:

  • Curriculum vitae.
  • Motivation letter.
  • Academic certificates or diplomas.
  • Evidence of professional experience.
  • Language certificates.
  • Other documents specifically requested in the vacancy notice.

Candidates should ensure that their documents clearly demonstrate how they meet the formal requirements and selection criteria.

Step 5: Submit Before the Deadline

Applications must be submitted through the official recruitment platform before the stated closing date and time.

ECDC does not accept applications submitted through alternative methods, such as email or post, unless the vacancy notice explicitly provides otherwise. After submitting an application, candidates should look for an automatic confirmation email and retain it for their records.

ECDC Recruitment and Selection Process

ECDC’s recruitment process generally involves several stages. The exact process may vary depending on the position, but the organisation outlines a typical sequence.

1. Application

Candidates submit an online application through the ECDC e-recruitment system.

2. Screening of Applications

ECDC reviews applications to determine whether candidates meet the formal eligibility requirements and whether their qualifications match the vacancy.

Candidates can generally check the status of their applications through the e-recruitment system. Only candidates selected for the next stage are contacted.

3. Written Test

Candidates who progress in the selection process may be invited to complete a written test remotely. The test is intended to assess relevant knowledge, analytical ability, technical competence, or other skills related to the position.

4. Panel Interview

Candidates may then be invited to a panel interview, usually conducted by video conference. ECDC indicates that interviews generally last between 45 and 60 minutes, although the duration may vary.

The selection panel is generally composed of several members and aims to reflect diversity in gender and nationality.

5. Document Validation

The selected candidate may be required to provide documentary evidence supporting the information included in the application. This may include academic qualifications, employment history, identity documents, and other required records.

The successful candidate may also be required to complete a declaration of conflict of interest.

6. Job Offer and Pre-Employment Requirements

After selection, the successful candidate receives a job offer. Under the applicable employment rules, the candidate may be required to undergo a mandatory medical analysis and physical check-up in Stockholm through ECDC’s selected medical service.

7. Reserve List

ECDC may establish a reserve list containing additional suitable candidates. The reserve list may be used if similar vacancies become available during its period of validity.

The recruitment process generally takes approximately three to four months, although the duration may vary depending on the vacancy and circumstances.

Learn More HERE.

Important Application Tips

Applicants interested in ECDC jobs should consider the following recommendations:

Match Your Profile to the Vacancy

Do not submit a generic application for every ECDC position. Tailor your CV and motivation letter to the specific job by highlighting:

  • Relevant academic qualifications.
  • Professional experience.
  • Technical and analytical skills.
  • Public health or sector-specific knowledge.
  • Project management experience.
  • Language abilities.
  • International or multicultural experience.
  • Evidence of achievements related to the role.

Read the Formal Requirements Carefully

A strong professional background does not replace mandatory eligibility requirements. Confirm that you meet the nationality, language, education, experience, and other conditions before applying.

Use Accurate Dates

Enter precise dates for education and employment history. Inaccurate or inconsistent information may create problems during document verification and could lead to disqualification.

Prepare Early

Begin preparing your documents before the application deadline. This is especially important when a vacancy requires academic certificates, employment confirmations, language evidence, or other supporting documentation.

Apply Only Through the Official Platform

ECDC requires candidates to submit applications through its official recruitment platform. Applications sent by email, post, or other methods are generally not accepted.

Monitor Your Application Account

After submitting an application, check your email and e-recruitment account regularly for updates, interview invitations, requests for documents, or other communication from ECDC.

Official Application and Further Information

Interested applicants should review current vacancies and submit applications through the official ECDC recruitment system.

  • Organisation: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control
  • Opportunity Type: Staff employment and career opportunities
  • Location: Stockholm, Sweden
  • Eligible Nationalities: Generally nationals of EU Member States, Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein
  • Application Deadline: Varies according to the specific vacancy
  • Application Method: Online through the ECDC e-recruitment platform
  • Official Recruitment Page: ECDC Staff Positions and Career Opportunities
  • ECDC Vacancies: View ECDC Vacancies
  • Recruitment Process: ECDC Recruitment Process
  • Candidate E-Recruitment Guide: ECDC Candidate E-Recruitment Guide
  • Recruitment Enquiries: recruitment@ecdc.europa.eu

Conclusion

ECDC staff positions provide qualified professionals with the opportunity to contribute to infectious disease prevention, public health preparedness, scientific analysis, and health protection across Europe. The Centre recruits individuals from diverse professional backgrounds, including epidemiology, public health, mathematical modelling, communications, IT, finance, administration, and other specialist fields.

Applicants should carefully review the requirements of each vacancy, confirm their eligibility, prepare a tailored application, and submit all required documents through the official ECDC e-recruitment platform before the stated deadline. Since deadlines and requirements differ by position, candidates should regularly monitor the official vacancies page for suitable opportunities.

Discover more global Internship and European opportunities on OFY.

item.content:encoded:
The Carnegie China Fellowship 2027 is now accepting applications from eligible American scholars, practitioners, journalists, lawyers, and other public intellectuals interested in developing original research on China’s rise, its global implications, and its relationship with the United States.

Organized through the University of Maryland School of Public Policy’s Center for International and Security Studies at Maryland (CISSM/CUSP context as presented in the fellowship guidelines), the one-year, non-residential fellowship is designed to connect rigorous research with public policy. Selected fellows receive a $20,000 stipend that can support activities such as teaching release, research-related travel, and research assistant compensation.

The fellowship provides an opportunity for researchers and professionals to investigate important questions concerning China while engaging with policymakers and the broader policy community in Washington and internationally. Fellows are expected to produce a policy-focused research paper and present their findings at the annual Carnegie China Conference at the University of Maryland.

Deadline: January 4, 2027

5

About the Carnegie China Fellowship

The Carnegie China Fellowship is a one-year, non-residential research fellowship intended to support rising American scholars and other qualified public intellectuals conducting research related to China.

The fellowship focuses on understanding:

  • China’s rise and development
  • The effects of China’s emergence on the wider world
  • China’s relationship with the United States
  • Issues of importance to public policy
  • Questions that can contribute to policymakers’ understanding of China and related global developments

Rather than limiting applicants to a single academic discipline, the program encourages proposals that approach China-related questions from different perspectives and that can communicate their findings beyond a narrowly specialized academic audience.

During the fellowship period, successful applicants are expected to undertake original, policy-oriented research and participate actively in the policy community. This can include engagement with policymakers in Washington and elsewhere.

The fellowship also requires fellows to produce a policy-focused research paper based on their work and present their findings at the annual Carnegie China Conference at the University of Maryland.

What the Carnegie China Fellowship Offers

One of the central components of the fellowship is a $20,000 stipend.

The stipend is intended to provide financial support that can help fellows dedicate time and resources to their proposed research project. According to the fellowship guidelines, the funding may be used for purposes such as:

  • Buying out teaching responsibilities
  • Research-related travel expenses
  • Research assistant compensation
  • Other activities directly connected to conducting the proposed research

Applicants should note that the fellowship does not provide all personal or research-related expenses. Fellows remain responsible for their own health insurance and for managing their own research-related travel logistics.

The fellowship also may not be deferred, meaning applicants should be prepared to undertake the fellowship during the designated period if selected.

Who Is Encouraged to Apply?

The Carnegie China Fellowship welcomes applications from a broad range of professionals whose work can contribute to a deeper understanding of China and its implications for international affairs and public policy.

The program specifically invites applications from:

  • Scholars
  • Practitioners
  • Journalists
  • Lawyers
  • Other public intellectuals

Applicants may come from different academic and professional backgrounds. The program specifically identifies areas such as:

Economics

Researchers working in economics may explore issues involving China’s economy, international economic relations, trade, development, financial systems, economic policy, or China’s role in the global economy.

Humanities

Applicants from the humanities may approach China-related questions through disciplines such as:

  • Area studies
  • Cultural studies
  • History
  • Related humanities fields

Historical and cultural research can qualify where the proposed project demonstrates meaningful relevance to public policy.

Law

Lawyers and legal scholars may propose projects examining China’s legal institutions, international law, regulatory developments, governance, or other legal questions connected to China and its relationship with the United States or wider world.

Social Sciences

The fellowship also welcomes researchers working in social sciences, including:

  • Anthropology
  • Political science
  • Sociology
  • Related social science disciplines

The program is not restricted to these fields, and applicants from other relevant areas may also apply.

The Fellowship Encourages Interdisciplinary Research

A notable feature of the Carnegie China Fellowship is its interest in projects that go beyond narrow disciplinary boundaries.

The program particularly welcomes research that:

  • Transcends narrow academic specialties
  • Moves beyond methodological debates that are primarily relevant within one discipline
  • Examines understudied issues
  • Connects academic research to broader public-policy questions
  • Can be communicated effectively to policymakers and non-specialist audiences

This means that applicants should think carefully about how their research can contribute to conversations outside their immediate academic field.

A strong proposal should make the significance of the research understandable to readers who may not have specialized knowledge of the applicant’s discipline.

Policy Relevance Is an Important Consideration

Applicants are expected to demonstrate the public-policy relevance of their proposed research.

Policy relevance does not mean that the project must be narrowly focused on current government policy. The guidelines specifically indicate that historical, sociological, and other forms of research can be relevant.

The important consideration is whether the project’s findings or lessons could help policymakers better understand an important topic.

Applicants should therefore explain clearly:

  1. What question their research will investigate.
  2. Why the question matters.
  3. What is original about the proposed research.
  4. How the research could contribute to understanding an issue of public importance.
  5. Why the findings could be useful to policymakers or the broader policy community.

Applicants should also be prepared to interact with policymakers in Washington as part of the fellowship experience.

Eligibility Requirements

The Carnegie China Fellowship has specific eligibility requirements.

Applicants must:

  • Be U.S. citizens.
  • Have received a PhD or JD from an accredited university.
  • Hold the qualifying degree at the time of application.
  • Submit a complete application in English.
  • Develop a research proposal that meets the fellowship’s requirements.

An institutional affiliation is not required to apply. This means that eligible applicants do not necessarily need to be currently affiliated with a university, research institution, or other organization.

The application form specifically asks applicants to provide information about their U.S. citizenship, PhD or JD qualification, awarding institution, year the degree was awarded, and primary academic discipline.

Who Is Not Eligible or What Projects Are Excluded?

The fellowship guidelines also identify several categories of applications and projects that will not be accepted.

The program will not accept:

  • Applicants currently working toward a PhD or JD
  • Partisan proposals
  • Advocacy-oriented proposals
  • Rewritten doctoral dissertations
  • Projects primarily involving the editing of texts, papers, or documents
  • Preparation of textbooks
  • Preparation of anthologies
  • Preparation of translations
  • Preparation of memoirs

Applicants should therefore ensure that their proposed project represents a distinct research undertaking rather than simply revising an existing doctoral dissertation or undertaking an editorial project.

The distinction between research and advocacy is particularly important. Applicants should formulate research questions objectively and demonstrate that their conclusions will emerge from the investigation rather than being predetermined.

Carnegie China Fellowship Selection Process

Applications that meet the initial eligibility requirements undergo a multi-stage review process.

The process includes internal evaluations by the relevant University of Maryland program and consideration by a selection committee that includes experts from inside and outside the University of Maryland.

The review process considers several dimensions of an applicant’s research and professional record.

1. Significance and Originality of the Research

Reviewers consider the importance of the proposed project and whether it offers an original contribution.

Applicants should therefore explain why their research question matters and what makes their proposed study different from existing work.

A proposal should make clear:

  • The problem being investigated
  • Why the problem deserves attention
  • What is already known
  • What remains unclear
  • What the applicant intends to discover
  • What new contribution the research could make

2. Policy Relevance

The proposal should explain how the research can contribute to policymakers’ understanding of the issue under investigation.

As noted in the guidelines, policy relevance does not require a project to be purely contemporary or governmental. Historical, sociological, cultural, and other research can qualify when its findings or lessons have potential relevance to public-policy understanding.

3. Quality of the Project Proposal

The quality of the proposal is another important consideration.

Applicants are encouraged to present their ideas with:

  • Clear definitions
  • Strong organization
  • Logical structure
  • Clarity
  • Appropriate scope
  • A clearly defined research problem
  • A coherent methodology
  • A persuasive explanation of the project’s importance

The proposal should explain what reviewers will learn from the research and why that knowledge matters.

Applicants are also encouraged to articulate a clear hypothesis or step-by-step argument around a central problem where appropriate.

4. Methodology

The research methodology should be clearly explained.

Applicants should identify:

  • The approach they intend to use
  • Why the chosen approach is appropriate
  • How they will gather the information or data required
  • What sources they will consult
  • What archives or collections they may use
  • What techniques will be used to analyze the evidence
  • How the methodology will allow them to address the research question

Because reviewers may come from fields different from that of the applicant, the proposal should explain specialized research methods in accessible language.

5. Applicant’s Capabilities and Achievements

The selection process also considers the applicant’s professional and academic record.

Applicants need to demonstrate that they possess the skills, knowledge, experience, and background necessary to complete the proposed project successfully.

However, the proposal should not present the project’s conclusion as predetermined.

Instead, applicants should demonstrate that the research involves a genuine inquiry and that there is something meaningful to investigate.

The application should give reviewers confidence that the proposed project is feasible and that the applicant has a realistic plan for completing it.

6. Contribution to CUSP’s Mission

The program also considers whether the candidate can contribute to the broader life, priorities, and mission of the center.

An important aspect of this is the ability to make expert research accessible to a broader audience.

Applicants should therefore consider how they can communicate their research beyond academic specialists and contribute to conversations connecting scholarship with public affairs.

Carnegie China Fellowship Application Requirements

All applications must be submitted online.

The program states that it will not accept application materials submitted by email or through other means, with the exception of the required reference letters, which are to be sent by the referees to the designated email address.

A complete application must be submitted in English.

Applicants are required to prepare the following materials:

1. Project Proposal

The project proposal is one of the most important components of the application.

It must:

  • Be no more than five single-spaced typed pages
  • Use 12-point type
  • Be submitted in PDF format
  • Clearly explain the proposed research project

The proposal should address several specific elements.

Detailed Description of the Topic

Applicants should provide a detailed explanation of the research topic and its importance.

The proposal should establish the central issue and explain why it deserves investigation.

Originality of the Study

Applicants must explain what makes their proposed study distinctive.

This can involve addressing an understudied question, approaching an established issue from a new perspective, examining new evidence, or developing a research approach that contributes something different.

Basic Ideas and Hypotheses

The proposal should explain the core ideas behind the research and identify the main hypotheses where appropriate.

The research question and argument should be sufficiently clear that a reviewer outside the applicant’s specific discipline can understand what the project is attempting to establish.

Methodology

The applicant should explain how the research will be conducted.

This includes describing the activities required to gather evidence and the methods that will be used to analyze the evidence.

Current Research Status

Applicants should also explain the current status of their research.

This should include information about:

  • Work already completed
  • Relevant collections or archives already consulted
  • Existing research or evidence gathered
  • What remains to be done
  • What the applicant expects to accomplish during the fellowship

This helps reviewers understand both the project’s current stage and how the fellowship would contribute to its completion.

2. Current CV or Resume

Applicants must submit a current CV or resume.

The CV/resume must not exceed three pages.

There is an important exception regarding publications, presentations, or events. A list of publications, presentations, or events placed at the end of the CV/resume does not count toward the three-page limit.

The CV should provide a clear overview of the applicant’s academic and professional background and demonstrate relevant achievements and capabilities.

3. Two Letters of Reference

Applicants must arrange for two letters of reference to be submitted by the deadline.

The letters should be written by people who are familiar with the applicant and their work.

Importantly, referees should receive a copy of the applicant’s project description so that their letters can address:

  • The proposed research
  • The applicant’s qualifications
  • The applicant’s ability to undertake the project
  • The applicant’s proposed contribution to the fellowship
  • How the applicant and/or their research could contribute to bridging academic learning and public affairs

The reference letters must be written in English.

Applicants are specifically advised not to submit letters originally written for another purpose, such as employment applications.

The applicant is responsible for ensuring that both reference letters reach the program by the application deadline.

Applicants are strongly encouraged to contact their referees before the deadline to confirm that the letters have been submitted.

Reference letters should be sent by the referees to:

cusp@umd.edu

Information Required in the Online Application

The online application form requests several categories of information.

Contact Information

Applicants are required to provide information including:

  • First name
  • Last name
  • Email address
  • Phone number
  • Permanent address
  • City or town
  • State or province
  • ZIP/postal code

Eligibility Information

The application asks applicants to affirm that:

  • They are a U.S. citizen.
  • They hold a PhD or JD awarded by an accredited institution.

Applicants must also provide:

  • Name of the awarding institution
  • Year the degree was awarded
  • Primary academic discipline

Project Information

Applicants must provide:

  • Project title
  • Project proposal

The proposal must be uploaded as a PDF and must comply with the five-page limit and formatting requirements.

The application specifies a 100 MB file limit for the proposal.

CV/Resume

Applicants must also upload their current CV or resume in PDF format.

The CV/resume is subject to the three-page requirement and has a stated 100 MB file limit.

Recommendation Confirmation

Applicants must confirm that they will request their two recommenders to submit their letters of recommendation to cusp@umd.edu by the deadline.

Applicants must also affirm that the information supplied in the application is true and accurate.

The form additionally asks applicants how they heard about the Carnegie China Fellowship.

Important Application Considerations

Prospective applicants should pay close attention to the distinction between a strong academic research proposal and a proposal written exclusively for specialists.

The Carnegie China Fellowship explicitly encourages applicants to make their projects understandable to individuals outside their own fields.

A proposal should therefore avoid unnecessary technical language and explain specialized concepts when they are necessary.

Applicants should focus on demonstrating:

  • A clearly defined research problem
  • An important and original research question
  • A logical research strategy
  • A suitable methodology
  • A realistic plan
  • Evidence of preparation and relevant expertise
  • Potential public-policy relevance
  • A willingness to engage with policymakers
  • The ability to communicate research findings to broader audiences

Why the Research Proposal Matters

The five-page proposal gives applicants limited space to communicate a substantial research project, making clarity and organization particularly important.

A well-structured proposal can help reviewers understand the relationship between the research question, methodology, evidence, expected contribution, and policy relevance.

Applicants should avoid treating the proposal simply as a summary of their previous academic work. The fellowship is intended to support a research project with its own purpose and contribution.

Similarly, applicants should avoid presenting a predetermined conclusion. The guidelines emphasize the importance of demonstrating that there is a genuine inquiry at stake.

Connecting Scholarship With Public Affairs

A central theme of the Carnegie China Fellowship is the relationship between research and public affairs.

The program is designed for people who can contribute rigorous knowledge while engaging with the policy community.

This makes the ability to communicate research findings beyond an academic audience an important component of the fellowship.

Selected fellows are expected to engage with the policy community in Washington and abroad and eventually present their findings at the annual Carnegie China Conference at the University of Maryland.

The fellowship therefore provides a structure in which research can move from academic investigation toward broader discussions involving policymakers and other public audiences.

Fellowship Timeline and Deadline

The current Carnegie China Fellowship application round is open now.

The application deadline is: January 4, 2027

The Carnegie China Fellowship 2027 offers eligible U.S. citizens with a PhD or JD an opportunity to undertake substantial research on China and its relationship with the United States while connecting scholarship with public policy.

item.content:encoded:
The Crustal Ocean Biosphere Research Accelerator (COBRA) is inviting applications for its 2027 Early Career Deep-Sea Expedition Leadership Master Class and Fellowship, an international training and professional development opportunity designed to prepare early career researchers and other emerging professionals to lead deep-sea research expeditions.

The 2027 COBRA Master Class will provide participants with practical knowledge and tools for planning deep-sea oceanographic field research from beginning to end. The programme covers the development of research concepts, funding and proposal writing, expedition preparation, at-sea operations, telepresence, permitting, reporting, data management, ocean law, and engagement with other researchers and stakeholders.

The 12-week programme combines synchronous online training with an in-person final week in Maine, United States. Selected participants will also become COBRA Fellows for the 2027 calendar year and will be eligible for additional COBRA leadership training opportunities.

Importantly, previous hands-on experience in deep-sea research, outreach, or policy is not required, making the opportunity accessible to early career professionals who want to build expertise in deep-sea science, exploration, research leadership, and ocean policy.

About the Crustal Ocean Biosphere Research Accelerator (COBRA)

The Crustal Ocean Biosphere Research Accelerator (COBRA) is an international research coordination network focused on accelerating research into the structure, function, resilience, and ecosystem services of the crustal ocean biosphere.

The network seeks to generate and coordinate research that can contribute to better decision-making, particularly in areas connected to:

  • Deep-sea mining
  • Subsea and subseafloor environments
  • Subsea carbon sequestration
  • Ocean exploration
  • Deep-sea ecosystems
  • Ocean science and policy

COBRA operates internationally and brings together researchers and other interested parties to strengthen research collaboration and improve the translation of scientific findings into practical decision-making.

COBRA is also an endorsed Action of the United Nations Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development.

COBRA’s Four Primary Activities

COBRA’s mission is organized around four primary activities:

1. Coordinate

COBRA brings together interested parties to identify research priorities and coordinate research planning.

This approach helps researchers and stakeholders work collaboratively rather than operating in isolation.

2. Accelerate

COBRA seeks to accelerate research by:

  • Leveraging research opportunities
  • Supporting research exchanges
  • Connecting researchers
  • Harnessing existing data
  • Encouraging collaboration

3. Translate

Scientific findings are most useful when they can inform decisions and be understood beyond the research community.

COBRA therefore works to translate research findings for:

  • Policymakers
  • Industry
  • The public
  • Other relevant stakeholders

4. Educate

The education component focuses on developing the next generation of ocean researchers and leaders.

The COBRA Master Class is the centerpiece of this education activity.

APPLY HERE

What Is the COBRA Master Class?

The COBRA Master Class is an intensive training programme designed to teach early career researchers (ECRs) how to plan a deep-sea expedition from start to finish.

Rather than focusing only on scientific theory, the Master Class provides practical training in the different stages involved in developing and carrying out deep-sea field research.

Participants will learn how to:

  • Develop research concepts
  • Plan deep-sea expeditions
  • Identify appropriate research assets
  • Develop funding proposals
  • Prepare for a research cruise
  • Plan operations at sea
  • Use telepresence for research and outreach
  • Understand permitting requirements
  • Prepare research reports
  • Manage data
  • Understand ocean law
  • Work collaboratively with other researchers and stakeholders
  • Communicate research findings to different audiences

Participants will also apply what they learn by developing an independent project during the programme.

Key Areas Covered During the Master Class

The training covers a broad range of skills required to successfully design, propose, conduct, and report deep-sea research.

1. Deep-Sea Research Assets

Participants will learn about the different types of assets and resources available for conducting deep-sea research and exploration.

Understanding available research assets is important when designing an expedition because researchers need to match their scientific objectives with appropriate equipment, platforms, vessels, and technologies.

2. Funding and Proposal Writing

The Master Class will provide guidance on:

  • Funding opportunities
  • Developing research proposals
  • Presenting research ideas
  • Building strong project concepts
  • Preparing proposals for potential funders

This component helps participants understand how scientific ideas can be transformed into fundable research projects.

3. Developing Research Concepts

Participants will learn how to develop research concepts while engaging with others in a respectful and reciprocal manner.

This emphasizes collaboration and meaningful engagement when developing research ideas.

4. Cruise Preparation

Planning a deep-sea expedition requires significant preparation before the vessel leaves port.

The Master Class will provide practical guidance on cruise preparation, helping participants understand what needs to be considered before an expedition begins.

5. At-Sea Operations Planning

Participants will learn about planning research activities while an expedition is underway.

This includes understanding how research operations can be organized to ensure that scientific objectives can be achieved during the available time at sea.

6. Telepresence for Research and Outreach

The programme also introduces participants to the use of telepresence in deep-sea research and public outreach.

Telepresence can allow researchers and audiences to engage with deep-sea research activities remotely.

7. Permitting and Reporting

Deep-sea research may involve regulatory and administrative requirements.

Participants will therefore learn about:

  • Permitting
  • Reporting requirements
  • Research-related documentation
  • Regulatory considerations

8. Data Management

Effective research requires appropriate management of the data generated during an expedition.

Participants will receive training related to data management, helping them understand how research data should be handled as part of a broader research project.

9. Ocean Law

The Master Class also introduces participants to ocean law, giving early career researchers exposure to the legal and policy dimensions of conducting research in marine environments.

International and Collaborative Focus

COBRA is an international network and seeks participation from people around the world.

The programme aims to build a broad collaborative pool of talent capable of contributing to deep-sea research that addresses societal needs.

Participants will learn from a variety of international subject matter experts. These instructors will provide specialist knowledge while also helping participants broaden their professional and research networks.

The programme is therefore not simply a classroom-based course. It is designed to create opportunities for:

  • Knowledge exchange
  • Collaboration
  • Professional networking
  • Interdisciplinary learning
  • Research leadership development
  • International engagement

2027 Partnership With the Schmidt Ocean Institute

The 2027 COBRA Master Class is sponsored by the Schmidt Ocean Institute.

As part of this sponsorship, COBRA will prioritize preparing participants to take advantage of the future cruise track and priorities associated with the RV Falkor (too).

This gives the 2027 programme a particular emphasis on preparing early career researchers to understand and potentially leverage opportunities associated with future deep-sea research expeditions.

Who Is Considered an Early Career Researcher?

COBRA uses a broad definition of Early Career Researcher (ECR).

Under the programme’s definition, an ECR may include:

  • A senior graduate student
  • A postdoctoral scientist
  • Junior faculty who are less than 10 years from their terminal degree
  • An early career employee of a government institution
  • An early career employee of a non-governmental organization or nonprofit
  • An early career employee of a company
  • Other junior professionals whose work is relevant to the programme

This broad definition means the opportunity is not limited exclusively to university researchers.

Early career professionals working in government, NGOs, nonprofits, companies, research institutions, and related organizations may also fall within the programme’s target group.

Previous Deep-Sea Experience Is Not Required

One of the notable features of the COBRA Master Class is that applicants do not need previous hands-on experience with deep-sea research, outreach, or policy.

This means that an applicant can be interested in entering or developing their career in deep-sea research and related areas without already having extensive practical expedition experience.

The programme is intended to help participants develop the skills required to become more capable researchers and research leaders.

Independent Project

Participants will have the opportunity to apply what they learn through the development of an independent project.

This provides a practical component to the training.

Instead of only receiving information through lectures and discussions, participants will use the knowledge and tools introduced throughout the Master Class to develop their own project.

This can help participants connect the different elements of expedition planning, research design, funding, operations, policy, data management, and communication.

COBRA Fellowship Status

Participants selected for the virtual Master Class will be considered COBRA Fellows for the 2027 calendar year.

Being designated a COBRA Fellow also makes participants eligible for additional COBRA leadership training opportunities.

Therefore, the programme extends beyond the 12-week Master Class itself by connecting selected participants with further leadership-development opportunities within COBRA.

Programme Format and Schedule

The 2027 COBRA Master Class will run for approximately 12 weeks, beginning in January 2027 and concluding in April 2027.

The programme combines:

  1. Synchronous virtual training
  2. Asynchronous learning
  3. Online networking
  4. An in-person final week

Virtual Training

The first 11 weeks will be conducted through synchronous online sessions.

The sessions will take place:

  • Every Tuesday
  • 12:00 PM–2:00 PM U.S. Eastern Time
  • Using Zoom

Applicants should take note of the U.S. time change mentioned in the announcement. On March 14, U.S. Eastern Time changes from UTC-5 to UTC-4.

In-Person Final Week

The final portion of the Master Class will take place in person at:

Bigelow Laboratory for Ocean Sciences
Maine, United States

The in-person component will take place:

April 12–14, 2027

Participants should also plan for travel days on:

  • April 11, 2027
  • April 15, 2027

Attendance at the in-person component is an essential requirement.

Asynchronous Learning and Networking

In addition to the weekly live sessions, participants will engage in asynchronous learning and networking.

These activities will be supported through:

  • The COBRA Master Class website intranet
  • A dedicated Slack channel

Participants are expected to complete approximately 30 minutes of asynchronous preparation each week.

This preparation will involve homework distributed through the Master Class website and/or Slack channel.

Weekly Participant Expectations

Each week of the virtual Master Class, participants are expected to:

1. Complete Preparation Work

Participants should dedicate approximately 30 minutes to asynchronous course preparation.

2. Attend the Live Session

Participants are expected to participate in the weekly live training and discussion session through Zoom.

The sessions will be recorded for internal distribution only.

The recordings are intended for participants who:

  • Cannot attend a particular class
  • Want to review the material
  • Want to refresh their learning

Discussion sections will not be made public because COBRA wants to protect vulnerable questions and conversations.

3. Participate in Slack Discussions

Participants will also be expected to communicate with instructors and other participants through the dedicated Slack channel.

This supports continued learning and networking outside the live classroom.

English Language Requirement

The virtual Master Class will be delivered in English.

Participants are expected to communicate in English.

However, the programme will use live transcription to support accessibility and language translation.

Although COBRA is an international network, the instructors are based in the United States. The course itself will nevertheless incorporate:

  • Non-U.S. resources
  • International programmes
  • Guest instructors
  • Perspectives relevant to different geographic contexts

Technology Requirements

Because much of the Master Class is conducted online, participants are expected to have access to their own:

  • Computer or other suitable computing device
  • Microphone
  • Camera
  • Internet connection

Participants should also be able to access and use their own:

  • Google account
  • Slack account
  • Zoom account
  • YouTube

However, COBRA recognizes that hardware and connectivity can be challenging for some participants.

Accommodations for hardware and connectivity support are available where needed.

Applicants who have difficulty meeting these technology requirements should therefore consider the available accommodation options rather than automatically assuming they cannot participate.

Travel Funding for the In-Person Component

Selected participants are eligible to receive travel funds to support their participation in the final in-person week of the Master Class in Maine.

Eligible travel costs include:

  • Transportation
  • Accommodation
  • Allowed per diem for meals

Travel expenses will be reimbursed after participants submit the required expense receipts.

Air Travel

For air travel, reimbursement is limited to economy/coach fares.

The announcement specifies that the most cost-effective route should be used.

Participants should therefore not assume that premium or business-class travel costs will be covered.

Visa Costs

Participants who require a visa to travel to the United States can have the visa costs funded.

However, obtaining the required visa remains the participant’s responsibility.

Participants are expected to work with their home institution to secure the necessary visas.

How Reimbursement Works

Eligible costs are reimbursed after participants submit the required expense receipts.

Payments can be offered through:

  • Bank account transfer, or
  • PayPal transfer

Participants must also submit the appropriate U.S. Internal Revenue Service form:

  • W-9, or
  • W-8, depending on taxpayer status

These forms are submitted to COBRA’s Managing Director as part of the reimbursement process.

Important: This Is Not an Employment Opportunity

The announcement makes an important distinction regarding the relationship between COBRA and Bigelow Laboratory for Ocean Sciences.

Participation in the 2027 COBRA Master Class does not constitute employment with Bigelow Laboratory for Ocean Sciences.

Bigelow Laboratory administers COBRA funding, but participation in the training should not be interpreted as a job or employment appointment at the laboratory.

Application Timeline

The 2027 COBRA Master Class follows the timeline below:

Date Activity
August 27, 2026 Application period opens
October 1, 2026 Application period closes and evaluation begins
November 16, 2026 Candidates notified of selection
January 12, 2027 Virtual Master Class begins
March 23, 2027 Virtual Master Class sessions end
April 11, 2027 Expected travel day
April 12–14, 2027 In-person conclusion at Bigelow Laboratory for Ocean Sciences
April 15, 2027 Expected return travel day

The supplied announcement describes the overall Master Class as running from January 12 to April 14, 2027, while the detailed schedule identifies March 23, 2027 as the end of the virtual Master Class and April 12–14 as the in-person conclusion.

Application Deadline

The application period closes on:

October 1, 2026

Applicants should submit their applications before the closing date and ensure that they can meet the programme’s mandatory participation requirements.

A Critical Participation Requirement

Prospective applicants should carefully consider their availability before applying.

COBRA specifically states that applicants should not apply if they cannot commit to both:

  1. The Tuesday synchronous virtual sessions from 12:00 PM–2:00 PM U.S. Eastern Time, and
  2. The final in-person week in Maine from April 12–14, 2027, including the associated travel days.

Both components are considered essential requirements of participation.

Therefore, applicants should confirm that they can attend the scheduled sessions and travel to the United States before submitting an application.

Visit HERE to learn about the COBRA Early Career Deep-Sea Expedition Leadership Master Class and Fellowship 2027

Who Should Consider Applying?

The Master Class is particularly relevant to early career professionals who want to develop their skills in:

  • Deep-sea research
  • Oceanography
  • Marine science
  • Ocean exploration
  • Expedition planning
  • Research leadership
  • Ocean policy
  • Environmental research
  • Science communication
  • Research project development
  • Marine conservation
  • Deep-sea governance

The opportunity is also relevant to junior professionals working outside traditional academic research environments, including those working for government agencies, NGOs, nonprofits, and companies.

Conclusion

The 2027 COBRA Early Career Deep-Sea Expedition Leadership Master Class and Fellowship is an international training and professional development opportunity focused on preparing the next generation of deep-sea research leaders.

Through 12 weeks of training, participants will learn how to move from developing a research concept to planning, proposing, executing, and reporting on deep-sea field research. The programme combines live virtual instruction, independent project development, asynchronous learning, professional networking, and an in-person conclusion at the Bigelow Laboratory for Ocean Sciences in Maine.

Participants will be exposed to topics ranging from funding and proposal writing to cruise preparation, at-sea operations, telepresence, permitting, data management, ocean law, and research communication. They will also learn from international subject matter experts and interact with a wider community of researchers and professionals.

Selected participants will become COBRA Fellows for the 2027 calendar year, providing access to additional COBRA leadership training opportunities. Travel support is also available for eligible costs associated with the required in-person component, including transportation, accommodation, permitted meal per diem, and visa costs where applicable.

Importantly, applicants do not need previous hands-on deep-sea research, outreach, or policy experience. The programme instead seeks to build the capabilities of early career researchers and professionals who can contribute to future deep-sea research and help connect ocean science with societal decision-making.

Interested applicants should carefully review the attendance requirements, technology requirements, English-language expectations, and travel commitments before applying. The application deadline is October 1, 2026.

For more global grants, scholarships, fellowships, internships, jobs, conferences, competitions, and other career opportunities for young people, visit the Opportunities for Youth (OFY) website at www.opportunitiesforyouth.org.

item.content:encoded:
The 2026 Dwabo Small Grants Programme is now open for applications from eligible civil society organisations in Ghana seeking financial support to implement innovative, locally grounded projects that promote the meaningful participation, economic empowerment and integration of persons with disabilities.

Launched by the Embassy of France in Ghana, the 2026 programme represents the sixth edition of the Dwabo Small Grants Programme and places a particular emphasis on economic inclusion and employability of persons with disabilities.

Successful projects can receive grants ranging from €8,000 to €10,000 for implementation over a 12-month period. The programme is designed to support practical initiatives that address barriers preventing persons with disabilities from accessing education, skills development, employment, entrepreneurship and sustainable livelihoods.

The application deadline is 23 September 2026 at 23:59. Both hard-copy and electronic submissions are required, and applicants must ensure that all required documents are submitted before the deadline.

About the 2026 Dwabo Small Grants Programme

The Dwabo Small Grants Programme is an initiative of the Embassy of France in Ghana intended to support projects that address important social and economic inclusion challenges.

For the 2026 edition, the programme focuses on improving the participation and economic integration of persons with disabilities. The call seeks projects that move beyond awareness alone and produce practical, measurable outcomes that can improve access to economic opportunities.

The programme is particularly interested in initiatives that:

  • Develop market-relevant skills for persons with disabilities.
  • Improve access to employment opportunities.
  • Support entrepreneurship and sustainable livelihoods.
  • Remove barriers to participation in the labour market.
  • Improve accessibility within educational and working environments.
  • Promote reasonable accommodation and assistive technologies.
  • Reduce stigma and misconceptions surrounding disability.
  • Strengthen disability-inclusive policies and institutional systems.
  • Build partnerships between disability organisations, civil society, government, employers and the private sector.

The French Embassy describes the programme as part of broader efforts to eliminate barriers to the economic empowerment of persons with disabilities and contribute to more inclusive societies. The initiative also contributes to Sustainable Development Goal priorities, particularly SDG 4 on Quality Education, SDG 8 on Decent Work and Economic Growth, and SDG 10 on Reduced Inequalities.

What the 2026 Dwabo Grant Supports

The programme is looking for innovative and locally implementable projects that can translate disability rights and inclusion principles into practical economic opportunities.

Projects may focus on one or several areas related to disability-inclusive economic participation.

1. Economic Empowerment and Employability

Projects can address barriers that prevent persons with disabilities from obtaining and retaining meaningful employment.

Potential interventions could include initiatives that improve employability, develop job-related skills, connect beneficiaries with employers or create more accessible pathways into the labour market.

The objective is to help persons with disabilities participate more meaningfully in economic activities rather than remain excluded from employment and income-generating opportunities.

2. Inclusive Education and Skills Development

The programme supports efforts to improve access to inclusive educational, vocational and other training environments, particularly from the secondary education level onwards.

Projects could therefore address gaps that prevent persons with disabilities from participating effectively in skills development programmes.

This may include improving the accessibility of training environments, strengthening inclusive teaching approaches or creating pathways between training and employment.

3. Accessibility and Reasonable Accommodation

Another priority is adapting educational and workplace environments to meet the accessibility requirements of persons with disabilities.

Projects may address:

  • Physical accessibility.
  • Reasonable accommodation.
  • Accessible learning environments.
  • Accessible workplaces.
  • Assistive technology.
  • Other practical measures that allow persons with disabilities to participate fully.

The focus is on identifying and reducing barriers that limit participation.

4. Awareness and Community Capacity

The programme also seeks to strengthen community awareness and capacity to identify and address barriers affecting the inclusion and economic participation of persons with disabilities.

Projects may therefore work with communities, employers, institutions or other stakeholders to improve understanding of disability inclusion and develop practical responses to exclusion.

5. Reducing Stigma and Stereotypes

Stigma, stereotypes and misconceptions about disability can create significant barriers to education, employment, entrepreneurship and skills development.

The 2026 call therefore supports initiatives designed to challenge misconceptions about the capabilities of persons with disabilities and encourage more inclusive attitudes and practices.

6. Legal, Policy and Institutional Frameworks

Projects may also contribute to strengthening legal, policy and institutional frameworks that promote disability-inclusive education, skills development, employment and economic participation.

This can involve working with relevant institutions and stakeholders to identify gaps and develop or strengthen approaches that support greater inclusion.

7. Partnerships for Economic Inclusion

The programme encourages collaboration among different stakeholders.

These can include:

  • Organisations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs).
  • Civil society organisations.
  • Public institutions.
  • Employers.
  • Skills-development institutions.
  • Private-sector organisations.
  • Local authorities.
  • Other relevant development partners.

Partnership-based projects can help create sustainable pathways into employment, entrepreneurship and broader economic participation.

Grant Amount and Project Duration

Successful applicants can receive between:

€8,000 and €10,000 per project

The grant supports projects implemented over:

12 months

Applicants should therefore develop realistic project plans that can be delivered within the specified implementation period.

The proposed budget should clearly correspond to the project’s activities, expected results and implementation requirements.

Who Can Apply for the 2026 Dwabo Small Grants Programme?

The opportunity is not designed for individual applicants.

The eligible applicants are legally registered civil society organisations operating in Ghana.

According to the published eligibility requirements, eligible organisations include:

  • Legally registered and recognised civil society organisations in Ghana.
  • Civil society organisations affiliated with established networks or coalitions.
  • Organisations with a regional or district-level presence in Ghana.
  • Organisations working with local partners to implement projects.
  • Organisations with demonstrated experience in disability inclusion, economic empowerment, employability, skills development, livelihoods, entrepreneurship, education, human rights or closely related areas.
  • Organisations with adequate organisational, technical and financial capacity to manage and account for grant funding.
  • Organisations with appropriate governance, financial management and internal control arrangements.

Geographic Eligibility

The 2026 Dwabo Small Grants Programme is Ghana-specific.

Therefore, the primary geographic eligibility is:

Country: Ghana

The applicant organisation must be legally registered and operating in Ghana.

This means that an individual from another African country, Europe, Asia, North America or another part of the world cannot apply simply as an individual.

Likewise, an international organisation would need to satisfy the programme’s specific requirements concerning eligible operations and partnerships in Ghana.

What Kind of Organisations Are Particularly Relevant?

Organisations whose existing work relates to disability inclusion and economic empowerment may be particularly relevant to this call.

Relevant organisational experience may include:

  • Disability rights and inclusion.
  • Economic empowerment.
  • Employment and employability.
  • Vocational and technical skills development.
  • Entrepreneurship.
  • Livelihood development.
  • Inclusive education.
  • Human rights.
  • Community development.
  • Accessibility.
  • Social protection and inclusion.
  • Workplace inclusion.

Applicants should be able to demonstrate that they have the organisational capacity and relevant experience necessary to implement the proposed project successfully.

Priority for Disadvantaged Regions

The programme indicates that preference will be given to projects implemented in disadvantaged regions, with particular emphasis on Northern Ghana.

Applicants planning projects in underserved communities should therefore clearly explain the local context, the barriers faced by persons with disabilities and how the proposed intervention will respond to those challenges.

However, applicants should still ensure that their project meets all eligibility and programme requirements rather than assuming that geographic location alone guarantees funding.

Co-Financing Requirement

Applicants are required to include at least 10% co-financing in their project proposals.

Co-financing can demonstrate that the proposed project has support beyond the Dwabo grant and may contribute to the sustainability of the intervention.

Potential sources of co-financing could include contributions from partners, other donors, private-sector organisations or other eligible sources, subject to the programme’s rules.

Projects that benefit from co-financing involving other partners may receive favourable consideration.

Possible partners can include:

  • NGOs.
  • Private-sector organisations.
  • Local authorities.
  • Other donors.
  • Community organisations.
  • Relevant institutions.

Important Budget Requirements

Applicants should pay close attention to the programme’s financial requirements when preparing their proposals.

Administrative and Operational Costs

Administrative and operational costs must not exceed 8% of the global project budget.

This means that the majority of the requested funding should be directed towards the actual implementation of project activities and achievement of intended results.

Equipment Costs

Equipment expenditure is limited to 7% of the total budget.

Applicants should therefore avoid developing proposals in which most of the requested funding is dedicated to purchasing equipment.

The proposal should instead demonstrate how resources will contribute directly to the project’s objectives and beneficiaries.

Sitting Allowances and Honoraria

The published requirements state that proposals should not include sitting allowances or honoraria.

Applicants should take this restriction into account when preparing their budgets.

Projects That Are Not Eligible

Not every type of activity qualifies for funding under the 2026 Dwabo programme.

Applicants should carefully distinguish between a project that contributes to disability-inclusive economic participation and an activity that falls outside the scope of the call.

The following types of actions are listed as ineligible:

Individual Participation in Events

Projects concerned only or mainly with individual sponsorship for participation in:

  • Workshops.
  • Seminars.
  • Conferences.
  • Congresses.

are not eligible.

Standalone Events

Projects focused only on organising workshops, seminars, conferences or congresses are also not eligible.

The programme is looking for substantive projects that produce meaningful inclusion and economic participation outcomes rather than simply financing events.

Individual Scholarships

Projects concerned only or mainly with individual scholarships for studies or training courses are not eligible.

This is an important distinction because the Dwabo programme is a project grant for eligible organisations, not an individual scholarship programme.

Formal Education

Projects in the formal education sector are generally ineligible except in special circumstances.

Applicants should therefore ensure that an education-related project clearly fits within the programme’s broader disability inclusion and economic participation objectives.

Political Party Activities

Actions supporting political parties are not eligible.

Religious Proselytism

Projects that include religious proselytism are not eligible.

Discriminatory Activities

Projects that discriminate against individuals or groups based on characteristics including:

  • Race.
  • Gender.
  • Sexual orientation.
  • Religious beliefs or lack of religious beliefs.
  • Ethnic origin.

are not eligible.

Activities Conflicting with Constitutional Provisions

Actions that conflict with constitutional provisions are also excluded.

These restrictions should be reviewed carefully before an organisation invests time in preparing its application.

What Should a Strong Project Proposal Demonstrate?

The programme expects applicants to present proposals that are clear, practical and measurable.

A strong proposal should clearly explain:

  1. The problem – What disability-related economic inclusion challenge exists?
  2. The target beneficiaries – Who will benefit from the project?
  3. The geographic area – Where will the intervention take place?
  4. The objectives – What does the project intend to achieve?
  5. The activities – What will the organisation actually do?
  6. The expected results – What measurable changes are expected?
  7. The indicators – How will progress and results be measured?
  8. The implementation plan – How will the project be delivered over 12 months?
  9. The budget – How will the grant and co-financing be used?
  10. The sustainability strategy – How will the benefits continue beyond the grant period?

The published requirements specifically call for clearly defined context, objectives, beneficiaries and measurable indicators, together with practical and innovative solutions that can be implemented locally.

Required Application Documents

Applicants should prepare the required documents before submitting their proposals.

The published application requirements include:

1. Completed Dwabo Grant Application Form

Applicants must complete the official grant application form provided for the 2026 call.

2. Completed Provisional Budget Form

The provisional budget must be completed in the required Excel format.

The budget should be:

  • Completed accurately.
  • Signed.
  • Stamped.
  • Consistent with the activities described in the proposal.

3. Official Bank Letter

Applicants must provide an official bank letter confirming the organisation’s Ghana Cedis account.

4. Certificate of Recognition

A valid Certificate of Recognition from the Department of Social Welfare is required.

5. Certificate to Commence Business

Applicants must provide a valid Certificate to Commence Business.

6. Certificate of Incorporation

A valid Certificate of Incorporation must also be submitted.

7. CVs of Key Project Team Members

Applicants must provide CVs for key project team members.

The CVs should not exceed three pages.

8. Letter of Support or Relevant Documentation

A letter of support or other relevant supporting documentation may also be submitted, with the supporting material limited to three pages.

All required documents should be valid for 2026.

Application Length and Formatting

Applicants should also follow the formatting requirements.

The application itself must not exceed:

8 pages, excluding annexes

The required font is:

Calibri, size 11

Applicants should therefore avoid unnecessarily lengthy narratives and focus on clearly explaining the problem, intervention, beneficiaries, activities, expected results, indicators, implementation arrangements and budget.

How to Apply for the 2026 Dwabo Grant

The 2026 Dwabo Small Grants Programme requires both hard-copy and electronic submission.

Applicants should prepare the complete application package and submit it through both required channels.

Hard-Copy Submission

The hard-copy application should be submitted at the Embassy’s security point in a sealed envelope.

The envelope should be addressed to:

Alberta AMEZIAH
Project Officer – Dwabo
Embassy of France
Fourth Circular Road
Cantonments, Accra, Ghana

Electronic Submission

Applicants must also submit the required documents electronically through the France Transfert platform.

The electronic submission must be completed before:

23 September 2026 at 23:59

The file should be named using the organisation’s name followed by:

DWABO 2026

The transfer package should be addressed to the project email specified in the call documentation.

Applicants should ensure that the electronic and hard-copy submissions are both completed before the deadline. The published requirements state that failure to submit both within the deadline will result in rejection of the application.

Application Resources

The official France in Ghana announcement provides three key application documents:

  • Dwabo Terms of Reference 2026 – contains the detailed programme requirements.
  • Grant Application Form – used to prepare the project proposal.
  • Provisional Budget – used to prepare the project budget.

Applicants should read the Terms of Reference carefully before completing the application because the detailed requirements determine whether a proposed project is eligible.

Key Information at a Glance

Item Details

Country Ghana
Implementing institution Embassy of France in Ghana
Grant amount €8,000–€10,000
Project duration 12 months
Main focus Economic inclusion and employability of persons with disabilities
Applicant type Legally registered civil society organisations
Geographic scope Ghana
Co-financing At least 10%
Administrative/operational costs Maximum 8% of global budget
Equipment costs Maximum 7% of total budget
Application length Maximum 8 pages excluding annexes
Font Calibri, size 11
Hard copy Required
