item.content:encoded:
The University of Edinburgh, through Edinburgh Law School and the Leverhulme Centre for Algorithmic Life, is inviting applications for a fully funded PhD studentship focused on the rapidly evolving relationship between artificial intelligence, algorithmic technologies, law and decision-making.

The opportunity is offered through the “Decisions” Cluster of the Leverhulme Centre for Algorithmic Life, with the successful candidate working with Professor Nehal Bhuta at Edinburgh Law School while also becoming part of the wider interdisciplinary research community of the Leverhulme Centre for Algorithmic Life, based at Durham University.

This PhD opportunity is particularly relevant to applicants interested in how algorithmic and AI technologies are transforming legal decision-making, governance, norms, accountability and responsibility. The research environment encourages collaboration across law, social sciences, humanities and sciences, making it potentially suitable for candidates whose interests extend beyond traditional disciplinary boundaries.

Applications must be submitted by 5pm on 30 September 2026.

About Edinburgh Law School

Edinburgh Law School is part of the University of Edinburgh and provides research opportunities across a broad range of legal and criminological subjects.

The School has an established community of approximately 100 PhD students, creating an environment in which doctoral researchers can participate in the intellectual and academic life of the institution while developing their own independent research.

According to the information provided by Edinburgh Law School, the School was ranked third in the UK for law for the quality and breadth of its research based on the 2021 Research Excellence Framework. The School also reports that 80% of its research outputs were rated as world-leading or internationally excellent, while its research environment received a 100% world-leading rating in the REF2021 exercise.

For prospective doctoral researchers, this provides an opportunity to undertake research within an established academic environment with access to experienced supervisors, research training and a wider community of scholars.

About the Fully Funded PhD Studentship

The studentship is part of the Decisions Cluster of the Leverhulme Centre for Algorithmic Life (CAL).

The successful candidate will be supervised by Professor Nehal Bhuta at Edinburgh Law School and will also be integrated into the wider research environment of the Leverhulme Centre for Algorithmic Life.

The centre takes an interdisciplinary approach to studying algorithmic technologies and their implications for human life, knowledge, perception and action.

One of the central questions guiding the centre’s research is how society should live with and alongside algorithmic technologies. Rather than focusing exclusively on individual technological projects, the centre examines broader and fundamental questions surrounding algorithmic life and how emerging technologies interact with social, legal and human systems.

This makes the studentship particularly relevant at a time when algorithmic systems are increasingly involved in areas such as public administration, welfare, security, military decision-making and other areas where decisions can have significant consequences for individuals and society.

What the Decisions Cluster Researches

The Decisions Cluster, led by Professor Nehal Bhuta, examines how algorithmic technologies are changing the nature and character of decision-making.

The cluster is interested in the interaction between human and algorithmic forms of knowledge and decision-making. As automated and machine-based systems become increasingly integrated into human institutions, questions arise concerning who or what makes decisions, how those decisions are justified, and how responsibility and accountability should be understood.

Research within the cluster considers areas including:

  • Algorithmic decision-making.
  • Artificial intelligence and law.
  • Automated decision systems.
  • Legal decision-making.
  • Accountability and responsibility.
  • Ethical approaches to automated decisions.
  • Norms and normativity.
  • AI-enabled military and security technologies.
  • Welfare and public administration.
  • Human-machine interactions in decision-making.
  • The changing role of legal concepts in algorithmic environments.

The cluster also seeks to develop new approaches to understanding decisions in an increasingly algorithmic world.

An important aspect of the research involves high-risk domains where automated technologies may influence decisions with substantial social, legal or political consequences. These include areas such as AI-enabled warfare, military technologies, security and public administration.

What the PhD Involves

A PhD at Edinburgh Law School is based on independent research culminating in the production of a substantial doctoral thesis.

The standard Edinburgh Law School PhD involves submitting a thesis of up to 100,000 words. The thesis is expected to constitute an original piece of research that makes a significant contribution to knowledge within the selected field and contains material of a standard suitable for publication.

For this particular studentship, the successful candidate will develop a research project connected to the broad themes of algorithmic technologies, AI, law and decision-making.

The precise research direction is expected to be developed through the application and subsequent academic discussions. Applicants are therefore encouraged to focus their proposal on clearly defined research questions and explain why those questions are important.

Interdisciplinary Research Environment

One of the distinctive features of this PhD studentship is its interdisciplinary character.

The opportunity is not limited to applicants following a conventional legal research pathway. The centre encourages researchers to develop their disciplinary expertise while collaborating with scholars from other academic fields.

Potential applicants may come from backgrounds including:

  1. Law and legal theory

    Candidates may be interested in how AI and algorithmic systems are changing legal concepts, legal reasoning, legal practice or legal decision-making.

  2. Socio-legal studies

    Researchers may explore how algorithmic systems influence institutions, social relationships, governance and the operation of law.

  3. Computer science

    A computer scientist could investigate machine learning and law, including the technical and social development of legal reasoning through algorithmic systems.

  4. Sociology

    Applicants with an interest in algorithmic social systems may explore theoretical questions concerning legal concepts, governance and social organisation.

  5. Humanities and social sciences

    Researchers from other relevant disciplines may investigate how algorithmic technologies are reshaping concepts of humanity, knowledge, responsibility, authority and decision-making.

The opportunity therefore provides scope for research that crosses traditional academic boundaries.

Funding and Financial Support

The studentship is described as a fully funded PhD opportunity for eligible applicants.

The funding package includes:

  • Tuition fees at the UK Home Fee rate.
  • An annual stipend in line with UK Research and Innovation rates, currently stated as approximately £21,805 per year.
  • Stipend payments made in equal monthly instalments.
  • Funding for 3.5 years, subject to satisfactory academic progress.
  • Additional research funding to support training and development.

The studentship is specifically restricted to candidates who qualify for Home fee status.

According to the opportunity information, eligible Home-fee candidates include applicants from the United Kingdom, Republic of Ireland, and EU-EEA applicants with Pre-settled status.

Applicants who do not meet the stated Home-fee eligibility requirements should carefully assess their fee status before applying, as the funding provided through this studentship is not described as covering international tuition fees.

Candidate Profile and Academic Requirements

The opportunity is aimed at applicants with a strong academic background and a demonstrable interest in the relationship between law and algorithmic or AI technologies.

Successful candidates are expected to have excellent grades in both undergraduate and postgraduate taught degrees, with at least one of those degrees being in law.

Applicants should also demonstrate a strong interest in questions concerning how AI and algorithmic technologies interact with law.

Relevant interests may include:

  • The influence of AI on legal decision-making.
  • Algorithmic governance.
  • The production and transformation of legal norms.
  • Normativity and algorithmic systems.
  • Automated decision-making.
  • Legal responsibility for decisions made or influenced by algorithms.
  • Accountability in AI systems.
  • The changing nature of legal practices.
  • AI and national legal systems.
  • AI and international law.
  • AI and global legal structures.
  • Algorithmic technologies in high-risk domains.

The School notes that any field of law may potentially be relevant, provided that the proposed research connects appropriately with the themes of the studentship.

English Language Requirements

Applicants must demonstrate proficiency in English, both written and spoken.

For candidates whose first language is not English, the stated requirement is an overall IELTS score of 7.0, with:

  • At least 7.0 in writing.
  • At least 6.5 in each of the other components.

The University may also accept another recognised English-language qualification at an equivalent standard.

Applicants should therefore ensure that they have appropriate evidence of English-language proficiency where this is required for their application.

Communication and Teamwork Skills

In addition to academic qualifications and research interests, applicants should demonstrate strong communication and teamwork skills.

Although a PhD involves substantial independent research, this particular studentship places the researcher within a wider interdisciplinary environment.

The successful candidate will have opportunities to engage with:

  • Other PhD researchers.
  • Postdoctoral researchers.
  • Academic collaborators.
  • Researchers from different disciplines.
  • University and research partners.
  • External partners in academia.
  • Industry partners.
  • Charitable organisations.
  • Arts-sector organisations.

The ability to communicate research ideas clearly and collaborate effectively across disciplinary boundaries can therefore be important to succeeding within the research environment.

Duration of the Studentship

The studentship is funded for 3.5 years, subject to satisfactory progress.

The precise duration may depend on the training requirements associated with the PhD project and any periods involving placement or collaborative work.

The successful applicant is expected to begin the PhD in either:

  • January 2027, or
  • September 2027.

Applicants should therefore consider their availability and preferred start period when preparing their application.

How to Apply

Applicants must apply through the University of Edinburgh’s admissions system, EUCLID, and select the PhD Law programme.

An important application instruction is that applicants should enter Professor Nehal Bhuta in the proposed supervisor section of the EUCLID application.

The application must be completed by 5pm on 30 September 2026.

Interviews are expected to take place online in late October 2026.

Applicants should make sure that all required documents are submitted before the deadline because incomplete applications will not progress to the academic selectors.

Required Application Documents

Applicants are expected to provide several documents as part of the application.

1. Degree Transcripts and Certificates

Applicants must submit their academic transcripts and degree certificates.

Where documents are not in English, certified translations should also be provided where applicable.

2. Evidence of English Language Ability

Applicants who are required to demonstrate English proficiency should provide the appropriate English-language qualification or evidence.

The stated IELTS requirement is an overall score of 7.0, including 7.0 in writing and at least 6.5 in each remaining component, unless an equivalent accepted qualification is used.

3. Research Proposal

Applicants must submit a short research proposal of no more than two pages.

The proposal should focus particularly on:

  • The research questions the applicant intends to investigate.
  • The proposed approach to the research.
  • Why the research questions are important.
  • How the proposed research relates to the broader themes of the studentship.

A strong proposal should therefore demonstrate a clear understanding of the research problem rather than simply providing a general discussion of artificial intelligence.

4. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must provide a full CV outlining their academic and professional background, research experience, relevant skills and other information that demonstrates their suitability for doctoral research.

5. Cover Letter

The application also requires a cover letter of no more than two pages.

The cover letter should explain:

  • The applicant’s academic and professional background.
  • Their suitability for the PhD.
  • Their research interests.
  • Their interest in the themes of the studentship.
  • Relevant experience that demonstrates their ability to undertake the proposed research.

6. Two Recent References

Applicants must provide two recent references.

It is the applicant’s responsibility to ensure that the reference letters are received before the application deadline.

Applicants should therefore contact their referees well in advance rather than waiting until the final days before submission.

Important Document Submission Requirement

The University provides an important instruction concerning the research proposal, CV and cover letter.

These three documents should be uploaded as one combined document within the application portal.

Applicants should therefore check the final uploaded file carefully before submitting the application to ensure that all required sections are included and readable.

The application should also contain all other required supporting documentation, including transcripts, certificates, English-language evidence where applicable and references.

Application Timeline

Key dates and expected stages include:

  • Application deadline: 5pm, 30 September 2026.
  • Interviews: Expected to take place online in late October 2026.
  • Potential PhD start: January 2027 or September 2027.
  • Funding duration: 3.5 years, subject to satisfactory progress.

Because the deadline is specific to the hour, applicants should not wait until the final minutes to submit their applications.

Who Should Apply?

This opportunity is particularly relevant to candidates who have a strong academic record and are interested in the intersection of law, artificial intelligence and algorithmic technologies.

Applicants should generally have:

  • Excellent undergraduate and postgraduate academic results.
  • At least one degree in law.
  • A demonstrable interest in AI and algorithmic technologies.
  • An interest in how these technologies interact with law and legal decision-making.
  • Strong written and oral English skills.
  • Strong communication and teamwork abilities.
  • An interest in interdisciplinary research.
  • The ability to develop a focused and meaningful doctoral research question.
  • Eligibility for UK Home fee status under the funding conditions.

The opportunity can potentially accommodate researchers from different disciplinary backgrounds, provided their proposed research connects meaningfully with the themes of algorithmic life, law and decision-making.

Eligible Countries and Fee Status

The funding is not open on an unrestricted worldwide basis.

The studentship is specifically available to applicants who qualify for UK Home fee status.

The information provided identifies eligible candidates as:

  • Applicants from the United Kingdom.
  • Applicants from the Republic of Ireland.
  • EU-EEA applicants with Pre-settled status, where they meet the relevant Home-fee eligibility requirements.

Applicants from other countries should not assume that they qualify for the funding simply because they meet the academic requirements. They should first establish whether they meet the University’s applicable Home-fee status requirements.

Why This Research Area Matters

Artificial intelligence and algorithmic technologies are increasingly influencing decisions that were traditionally made exclusively by humans.

These developments create significant questions for law and society.

For example, when an algorithm contributes to a decision, questions may arise concerning who is responsible for the outcome, how the decision can be challenged, whether the reasoning behind it can be explained, and what legal standards should govern the use of automated systems.

These questions become particularly significant in areas where decisions can affect people’s rights, access to services, security or welfare.

The Decisions Cluster provides an academic environment for investigating these issues at a fundamental level. Researchers can examine not only how algorithmic systems operate but also how concepts such as responsibility, accountability, ethics and legal decision-making may need to evolve alongside technological change.

Research Training and Support at Edinburgh Law School

PhD students at Edinburgh Law School benefit from a structured research environment designed to support both specialist research and broader academic development.

The School’s PhD programme provides:

  • Expert supervision in the candidate’s research area.
  • Training in legal and criminological research methods.
  • Transferable research and professional skills.
  • Opportunities for advanced specialist training.
  • Interaction with established researchers.
  • Participation in a wider scholarly community.
  • Opportunities to communicate research findings to different audiences.

The broader Leverhulme Centre environment also offers opportunities for interdisciplinary engagement, allowing doctoral researchers to develop connections beyond their primary academic discipline.

Career Development Opportunities

The PhD is designed not only to develop advanced research expertise but also to contribute to the candidate’s longer-term professional development.

Researchers can benefit from specialist training and engagement with academic and external partners.

The wider Edinburgh Law School PhD community includes graduates who have pursued careers in different areas, including:

  • Academic careers in law and criminology.
  • Private legal practice.
  • National governments.
  • International organisations.
  • Research and policy-related careers.

For researchers working at the intersection of law and emerging technologies, interdisciplinary experience may also provide a foundation for engaging with organisations and institutions dealing with AI governance, technology policy, regulation and algorithmic decision-making.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Applicants should begin preparing their application well before the deadline.

A useful preparation process is to:

  1. Review the research themes carefully.
    Make sure your proposed topic genuinely connects with algorithmic technologies, law and decision-making.
  2. Develop focused research questions.
    The proposal is limited to two pages, so applicants should prioritise clear and researchable questions rather than attempting to cover an overly broad subject.
  3. Explain why the research matters.
    Demonstrate the legal, theoretical, social or practical importance of the proposed research.
  4. Demonstrate interdisciplinary potential.
    If your research draws on computer science, sociology, political science, philosophy or another field, clearly explain how that discipline contributes to the project.
  5. Check your academic eligibility.
    Confirm that you meet the required academic standards and that at least one of your undergraduate or postgraduate taught degrees is in law.
  6. Check your fee-status eligibility.
    Because the funding is restricted to Home fee-status candidates, this should be established before submitting the application.
  7. Prepare your references early.
    Contact referees in advance and ensure they understand the submission deadline.
  8. Combine the required documents correctly.
    The research proposal, CV and cover letter should be uploaded as one combined document.
  9. Review the entire application.
    Missing documents can prevent an application from progressing to academic selection.
  10. Submit before the deadline.
    The application deadline is 5pm on 30 September 2026.

APPLY HERE

About the Edinburgh Law School PhD Programme

Beyond this specific studentship, Edinburgh Law School offers PhD study across an extensive range of legal and criminological subjects.

The general PhD programme can be studied:

  • Full time over three years, or
  • Part time over six years, subject to applicable visa restrictions.

Edinburgh Law School accepts applications for PhD study commencing in either September or January.

The School also offers an LLM by Research, providing another route for applicants interested in advanced legal research.

For candidates considering doctoral research outside the specific funded studentship, the School’s research areas can help identify potential supervisors and relevant research communities.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Fully Funded PhD Studentship at Edinburgh Law School 2026.

Deadline

The deadline for the Fully Funded PhD Studentship – Leverhulme Centre for Algorithmic Life, Decisions Cluster is: 5pm on 30 September 2026.

Applicants should ensure that all supporting documents, including references, are received before the deadline.

Application Link

Applicants should submit their application through the University of Edinburgh’s postgraduate admissions system and select the PhD Law programme. In the proposed supervisor section, applicants should enter Professor Nehal Bhuta.

Official information and application details are available through the University of Edinburgh and Edinburgh Law School.

Conclusion

The Fully Funded PhD Studentship at Edinburgh Law School offers an opportunity for eligible Home-fee-status candidates to undertake advanced doctoral research into the relationship between artificial intelligence, algorithmic technologies, law and decision-making.

The studentship provides UK Home tuition fees, an annual stipend of approximately £21,805, additional research and training support, and funding for 3.5 years subject to satisfactory progress. The successful researcher will work with Professor Nehal Bhuta and become part of the interdisciplinary research environment of the Leverhulme Centre for Algorithmic Life.

With research interests spanning algorithmic decision-making, legal responsibility, accountability, AI and law, automated systems and high-risk decision environments, the opportunity is suited to academically strong candidates who want to investigate how emerging technologies are transforming legal and social systems.

Interested applicants should carefully review the academic, English-language and Home-fee-status requirements, prepare the required research proposal and supporting documents, arrange their references early, and submit a complete application through EUCLID before 5pm on 30 September 2026.

item.content:encoded:
The Public Policy and International Affairs (PPIA) Junior Summer Institute 2027 is inviting eligible undergraduate students to apply for a fully funded summer programme designed to prepare emerging leaders for graduate study and careers in public policy, international affairs, public administration, and public service.

Through this intensive summer experience, selected participants will study at one of three leading institutions: Harvard University, Princeton University, or the University of Michigan. Fellows will undertake graduate-level coursework, develop analytical and policy skills, receive financial support, explore public service career pathways, and join a lifelong community of students and professionals committed to improving society.

The application deadline is November 6, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time.

Overview of the PPIA Junior Summer Institute

The PPIA Junior Summer Institute, commonly known as JSI, is a rigorous summer programme for undergraduate students who are approaching the final year of their degree and are interested in pursuing graduate education and professional careers connected to public service.

The programme is intended to help students understand how public policy is developed, how governments and institutions respond to social challenges, and how research, economics, statistics, leadership, communication, and policy analysis can be used to address real-world problems.

The 2027 programme will be hosted at:

  1. Harvard University – Harvard Kennedy School
  2. Princeton University – School of Public and International Affairs
  3. University of Michigan – Gerald R. Ford School of Public Policy

PPIA describes the Junior Summer Institute as a fully funded summer experience that combines academic preparation, professional development, career guidance, financial support, and community-building. The official programme page confirms that participating Fellows receive support covering major aspects of the summer experience, including coursework, housing, books, and a stipend.

Key Details at a Glance

Detail Information
Programme PPIA Junior Summer Institute
Programme year Summer 2027
Opportunity type Fully funded fellowship and summer institute
Main focus Public policy, international affairs, public service, leadership, and graduate school preparation
Host institutions Harvard University, Princeton University, and University of Michigan
Location United States
Application deadline November 6, 2026
Deadline time 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time
Programme duration Approximately six to seven weeks, depending on the host institute
Target applicants Undergraduate juniors preparing for their final year
Funding Tuition, housing, books or course materials, stipend, and other support depending on the host institute
Application method Online application through the PPIA application portal

What Does the PPIA Junior Summer Institute Offer?

The programme offers more than a traditional summer course. It is structured to provide academic training, professional preparation, financial assistance, mentorship, and access to a broader public service community.

1. Fully Funded Summer Experience

One of the most important benefits of the PPIA Junior Summer Institute is its financial support.

The programme is designed to reduce common financial barriers that may prevent talented students from accessing intensive academic and professional development opportunities.

The official PPIA programme information identifies the following forms of support:

  • Summer stipend.
  • Funded graduate-level coursework.
  • On-campus housing.
  • Books and related course materials.
  • Career coaching and professional guidance.
  • Additional support that may vary by host institution.

The precise structure and value of financial support may differ among the participating universities. Applicants should review the details provided by their selected JSI school before applying.

At Harvard Kennedy School, for example, the 2027 programme information states that participants receive full tuition, housing and meals, reimbursement for domestic travel to and from the programme, books and related course materials, and a US$2,000 stipend for summer living expenses.

2. Graduate-Level Coursework

PPIA Fellows participate in challenging coursework designed to introduce them to the academic expectations of graduate programmes in public policy and international affairs.

Depending on the host institution, coursework may cover areas such as:

  • Public policy.
  • Public administration.
  • International affairs.
  • Economics.
  • Statistics.
  • Quantitative analysis.
  • Policy research.
  • Policy writing.
  • Leadership.
  • Public speaking.
  • Policy design.
  • Government and governance.
  • International economics.
  • Foreign policy.
  • Diplomacy.
  • Education policy.
  • Economic policy.

The coursework is intended to help participants develop the academic foundation required for future graduate study.

Students may also gain experience interpreting evidence, examining policy choices, writing analytical documents, presenting arguments, and applying research methods to real-world public problems.

3. Preparation for Graduate School

A central objective of the PPIA Junior Summer Institute is to prepare undergraduate students for graduate education.

The programme helps participants understand:

  • What graduate-level policy study involves.
  • How to evaluate graduate programmes.
  • How to prepare for graduate applications.
  • What academic skills are needed for policy-related degrees.
  • How to identify areas of specialization.
  • How to connect undergraduate experiences with future academic goals.
  • How to prepare for careers in public service and related fields.

PPIA Fellows may also receive access to graduate school application support, application fee waivers, and scholarship opportunities through PPIA’s Graduate School Consortium.

The exact benefits available after completing JSI depend on the participating graduate school and its policies. Some PPIA partner institutions offer financial awards to eligible Fellows who later gain admission to relevant graduate programmes.

At Harvard Kennedy School, students who successfully complete a PPIA Junior Summer Institute and later gain admission to an eligible degree programme at Harvard Kennedy School may apply for at least a US$5,000 scholarship, subject to the applicable conditions.

4. Career Coaching and Professional Guidance

The programme provides guidance to help students connect their academic interests with future professional opportunities.

Career development may include:

  • Exploring careers in government.
  • Understanding opportunities in nonprofit organizations.
  • Learning about international and humanitarian institutions.
  • Examining careers in public administration.
  • Developing professional goals.
  • Identifying graduate programmes.
  • Strengthening résumés and personal statements.
  • Learning how to communicate policy interests.
  • Understanding the relationship between academic preparation and public service careers.

This support can be particularly useful for students who are interested in public service but are still deciding whether to pursue careers in government, international development, research, advocacy, nonprofit management, diplomacy, or policy analysis.

5. Housing and Course Materials

The PPIA Junior Summer Institute provides participating Fellows with university housing and course materials as part of its funded summer experience.

The official PPIA page specifically lists:

  • Housing.
  • Books.
  • Funded coursework.
  • Summer financial support.

Housing allows participants to live within the university environment and engage more fully in academic and community activities. Course materials help Fellows focus on their studies without having to bear the full cost of required resources.

The precise accommodation and meal arrangements may differ depending on the host institution.

6. A Lifelong Professional and Peer Community

PPIA brings together students who share an interest in public service, policy, leadership, and social impact.

During the programme, Fellows can build relationships with:

  • Students from different academic and personal backgrounds.
  • Faculty members.
  • Policy professionals.
  • Public service practitioners.
  • Graduate school representatives.
  • Alumni.
  • Researchers.
  • Leaders from government and nonprofit organizations.

The relationships formed during JSI can continue beyond the summer through the PPIA alumni network and graduate school community.

PPIA’s wider alumni network includes thousands of individuals pursuing careers and further study in public policy, international affairs, public administration, nonprofit leadership, and related fields.

Participating Universities and Their Areas of Focus

Applicants may study at one of three participating institutions. Each host university offers its own academic environment, faculty expertise, curriculum, and approach to public service.

Harvard University – Harvard Kennedy School

The Harvard Kennedy School JSI focuses on preparing undergraduate students for graduate study and careers in public policy and international affairs.

Potential areas of study include:

  • Economic policy.
  • Public policy.
  • Government.
  • Economics.
  • Statistics.
  • Policy design.
  • Policy analysis.
  • Leadership.
  • Race and racism in policy contexts.
  • Communication and analytical reasoning.

Harvard’s programme also includes a policy-focused incubator experience in which students may work in small groups to examine a policy issue, develop solutions, prepare policy memos, produce professional reports, and deliver presentations supported by data visualization.

The Harvard programme is held in Cambridge, Massachusetts, within the Boston metropolitan area.

The official Harvard information indicates that its 2027 JSI is scheduled to run from June 13 to July 30, 2027.

Princeton University – School of Public and International Affairs

Princeton’s JSI is hosted by the School of Public and International Affairs.

Its areas of emphasis include:

  • International economics.
  • Foreign policy.
  • Diplomacy.
  • Public policy.
  • International affairs.
  • Statistics.
  • Economics.
  • Policy research.
  • Policy writing.
  • Public speaking.
  • Leadership.

Princeton’s programme includes a policy workshop that examines a domestic policy or international affairs issue. Participants develop research skills, write policy memos, use economics and statistics in policy reports, and deliver group presentations.

Princeton’s official application information states that applicants must demonstrate an interest in and commitment to a career in public or international affairs. It also requires relevant coursework, such as college-level economics, mathematics, or statistics, or equivalent AP or IB coursework.

University of Michigan – Gerald R. Ford School of Public Policy

The University of Michigan’s JSI is hosted by the Gerald R. Ford School of Public Policy.

Its listed areas of focus include:

  • Public policy.
  • Economic policy.
  • Education policy.
  • Policy analysis.
  • Public service.
  • Leadership.
  • Research and communication.

The University of Michigan provides an academic environment where students can explore policy questions, develop analytical abilities, and understand how public policy affects communities and institutions.

Applicants should review the current programme information for the University of Michigan to understand its specific curriculum, eligibility requirements, and financial support arrangements.

Academic and Professional Skills Participants Can Develop

The PPIA Junior Summer Institute is intended to strengthen a broad range of skills that are relevant to graduate study and public service careers.

Policy Analysis

Participants learn how to examine public problems, assess policy alternatives, interpret evidence, and communicate recommendations.

Economics and Statistics

Many public policy and international affairs programmes require students to understand economic reasoning and quantitative evidence. JSI helps participants strengthen their foundation in these areas.

Research Skills

Fellows may learn how to:

  • Identify credible sources.
  • Examine policy evidence.
  • Conduct structured research.
  • Interpret data.
  • Develop research questions.
  • Apply analytical methods.
  • Prepare policy-oriented reports.

Policy Writing

Participants may gain experience preparing:

  • Policy memos.
  • Research summaries.
  • Analytical reports.
  • Policy recommendations.
  • Professional presentations.
  • Written arguments supported by evidence.

Leadership and Collaboration

The programme encourages Fellows to work with peers from different backgrounds and perspectives. This can strengthen:

  • Teamwork.
  • Communication.
  • Negotiation.
  • Problem-solving.
  • Public speaking.
  • Collaborative leadership.
  • Interpersonal skills.

Professional Communication

Participants may develop the ability to explain complex policy issues clearly to different audiences, including policymakers, researchers, community members, nonprofit leaders, and the general public.

Who Can Apply?

The PPIA Junior Summer Institute is designed primarily for undergraduate students who are approaching the final year of their degree and are interested in graduate study and public service careers.

The general programme profile includes students who:

  • Have junior standing at the time of application.
  • Will have one or two semesters remaining after completing the summer institute.
  • Are enrolled at an accredited college or university.
  • Demonstrate an interest in public policy, international affairs, public administration, or related fields.
  • Are committed to pursuing graduate education in a relevant discipline.
  • Demonstrate a commitment to public service.
  • Are interested in contributing diverse perspectives to policy and public affairs discussions.

Students from many academic disciplines may be considered. The programme is not limited to political science, economics, public administration, or international relations majors.

Depending on the host institution, applicants may come from fields such as:

  • Education.
  • Management.
  • Business.
  • Economics.
  • Political science.
  • Sociology.
  • History.
  • Law.
  • International studies.
  • Environmental studies.
  • Public health.
  • Engineering.
  • Data science.
  • Communications.
  • Humanities.
  • Social sciences.
  • Other academic disciplines.

The key consideration is whether the applicant can demonstrate an interest in public service, policy, community improvement, and future graduate study.

Eligibility Requirements

Eligibility requirements may vary by participating institution. Applicants should review the current PPIA requirements and the rules of their preferred JSI school before submitting an application.

Common requirements may include the following:

1. Undergraduate Junior Standing

Applicants are generally expected to be college juniors at the time of application or to have junior standing and return to their undergraduate studies after the summer programme.

Students who will have already completed their bachelor’s degree before the programme begins may not be eligible.

2. Remaining Undergraduate Study

Applicants should normally have one or two semesters of undergraduate study remaining after completing JSI.

The programme is intended to take place before the student’s final undergraduate year.

3. Interest in Public Service

Applicants should demonstrate an interest in pursuing a career connected to public service.

Relevant areas may include:

  • Government.
  • Public administration.
  • Public policy.
  • International affairs.
  • Diplomacy.
  • Humanitarian organizations.
  • Nonprofit organizations.
  • International development.
  • Community development.
  • Social policy.
  • Education policy.
  • Environmental policy.
  • Public health policy.
  • Research and public leadership.

4. Commitment to Graduate Study

PPIA is designed for students who intend to pursue graduate education in public policy, public administration, international affairs, or a related field.

Applicants should be able to explain how JSI fits into their longer-term academic and professional plans.

5. Relevant Coursework or Experience

Some participating institutes require or recommend coursework in economics, mathematics, or statistics.

For example, Princeton’s eligibility information requires applicants to have completed at least one course in college-level economics, mathematics, or statistics, or an equivalent AP or IB course. Applicants may also demonstrate relevant preparation through their academic background and public service interests.

Other relevant preparation may include:

  • Public policy coursework.
  • Research experience.
  • Internships.
  • Volunteer work.
  • Community leadership.
  • Student organization involvement.
  • Public service projects.
  • Work experience connected to social or public issues.

6. Citizenship and Residency Requirements

Citizenship and residency requirements may differ depending on the host institute.

U.S. citizens, permanent residents, and DACA recipients may be eligible for participating PPIA institutes. International students may be eligible for selected institutes, provided they are enrolled at an accredited U.S. institution and meet the relevant requirements.

For example, Princeton’s official application page states that international students pursuing an undergraduate degree at an accredited U.S. four-year college or university may apply if they meet the programme’s eligibility requirements.

Applicants should not assume that eligibility for one JSI school automatically guarantees eligibility for all participating institutions.

Is the Programme Open to All Academic Majors?

Yes. The PPIA Junior Summer Institute is not restricted to one academic major.

Students from a variety of academic backgrounds are encouraged to consider applying if they are interested in public service and graduate study.

Applicants from non-quantitative majors should not automatically assume they are ineligible. Harvard’s programme information, for example, indicates that students from different academic backgrounds may apply and that the programme is intended to help participants develop the skills needed for graduate policy study.

However, applicants should review the requirements of the specific institution they select, particularly where coursework in economics, mathematics, or statistics is required.

Financial Support and Programme Benefits

The PPIA Junior Summer Institute’s funding package is designed to allow Fellows to focus on learning and professional development.

Depending on the host institute, support may include:

  • Full tuition.
  • University housing.
  • Meals or a meal plan.
  • Books.
  • Course materials.
  • Summer stipend.
  • Travel assistance.
  • Career coaching.
  • Graduate school preparation.
  • GRE preparation or related resources.
  • Graduate school application fee waivers.
  • Access to scholarship opportunities.
  • Alumni networking.
  • Mentorship and professional development.

Not every benefit is necessarily identical across the three host universities. Applicants should confirm the financial support available at their preferred institution.

Example of Harvard Financial Support

For the 2027 Harvard Kennedy School JSI, the published information lists:

  • Full tuition.
  • Housing and meals.
  • Reimbursement for domestic travel to and from the programme.
  • Books and related course materials.
  • A US$2,000 stipend for summer living expenses.
  • GRE preparation and preparation materials.
  • Potential eligibility for at least a US$5,000 scholarship if the Fellow later gains admission to an eligible Harvard Kennedy School degree programme.

These post-programme scholarship benefits are subject to the applicable requirements and should not be interpreted as automatic admission or guaranteed funding for every graduate programme.

Programme Duration and Timing

The PPIA Junior Summer Institute is an intensive summer programme. The duration may vary slightly by participating university, but the experience generally lasts approximately six to seven weeks.

The programme combines:

  • Classroom instruction.
  • Graduate-level coursework.
  • Workshops.
  • Policy research.
  • Group projects.
  • Career development.
  • Networking.
  • Professional and community activities.

The 2027 programme will take place during the summer before participants complete their final year of undergraduate study.

Applicants should ensure that they are available for the full programme period and understand that JSI requires a substantial commitment of time and participation.

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the PPIA Junior Summer Institute 2027 is:

November 6, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time.

Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline and avoid waiting until the final hours, particularly because supporting documents and recommendation letters may require additional time.

The official PPIA programme page confirms the deadline as November 6, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time.

Application Requirements

The exact application requirements may vary by institution, but applicants should be prepared to provide several materials.

Common application materials may include:

  • Completed online application form.
  • Résumé or curriculum vitae.
  • Personal statement.
  • Academic transcripts.
  • Information about coursework.
  • Details of internships, work experience, volunteering, and extracurricular activities.
  • Information about community involvement.
  • Two letters of recommendation.
  • Financial information, where requested.
  • Financial aid documents, where applicable.
  • Responses explaining academic and career goals.
  • Information about public service interests.

Princeton’s application information lists a résumé, a multipart personal statement, unofficial academic transcripts from all colleges and universities attended, two recommendation letters, financial information, and the completed PPIA JSI application among its requirements.

Applicants should consult the official application portal for the most current list of required documents.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should follow these steps:

  1. Visit the Official PPIA Junior Summer Institute website.
  2. Review the general programme information and eligibility requirements.
  3. Explore the participating host institutions: Harvard, Princeton, and the University of Michigan.
  4. Review the eligibility and financial support information for the institution you are interested in.
  5. Prepare your résumé, transcripts, personal statement, and other required materials.
  6. Contact potential recommenders early and request recommendation letters.
  7. Complete the Online Application.
  8. Upload all required documents.
  9. Review the application carefully for accuracy and completeness.
  10. Submit the application before November 6, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time.

Official Application Portal

Applications can be submitted through the official PPIA application platform:

Apply for the PPIA Junior Summer Institute 2027

Official Programme Website

For programme details, participating institutions, eligibility information, and application updates, visit:

PPIA Junior Summer Institute

Virtual Application Seminars

PPIA is offering virtual seminars to help prospective applicants understand the Junior Summer Institute and prepare their applications.

These sessions are designed to provide information about:

  • The purpose of the programme.
  • Eligibility requirements.
  • The application process.
  • Personal statements.
  • Supporting materials.
  • The student experience.
  • Coursework and career preparation.
  • Questions from prospective applicants.

The listed virtual sessions include:

Your Summer, Your Future

  • Date: September 23, 2026
  • Time: 6:00–7:00 p.m. Eastern Time
  • Format: Virtual
  • Focus: Introduction to PPIA and the Junior Summer Institute, including programme benefits, eligibility, and the application process.

Inside the Junior Summer Institute

  • Date: October 6, 2026
  • Time: 6:00–7:00 p.m. Eastern Time
  • Format: Virtual
  • Focus: Experiences shared by former or current JSI Fellows, including coursework, friendships, and the overall summer experience.

Put Your Best Application Forward

  • Date: October 19, 2026
  • Time: 4:00–5:00 p.m. Eastern Time
  • Format: Virtual
  • Status: Tentative
  • Focus: Practical guidance from institute directors on communicating interests, experiences, and goals, understanding application requirements, and avoiding common mistakes.

Applicants should check the official PPIA website for registration details, updates, and any changes to the seminar schedule.

How to Prepare a Competitive Application

Applicants can strengthen their applications by presenting a clear connection between their experiences, academic interests, public service goals, and future plans.

1. Explain Your Interest in Public Service

Describe the public issues you care about and why you want to contribute to solving them.

Possible areas may include:

  • Education inequality.
  • Poverty reduction.
  • Public health.
  • Climate change.
  • Economic development.
  • Human rights.
  • Governance.
  • Migration.
  • International development.
  • Social protection.
  • Community development.
  • Youth empowerment.
  • Public administration.
  • Education policy.

2. Demonstrate Relevant Experience

Applicants can draw on experiences such as:

  • Internships.
  • Research projects.
  • Volunteer work.
  • Student leadership.
  • Community initiatives.
  • Employment.
  • Advocacy.
  • Public service activities.
  • Campus organizations.
  • Social impact projects.

Experience does not have to come from a formal government position. Community involvement and sustained responsibility can also demonstrate commitment to public service.

3. Connect Your Academic Background to Your Goals

Explain how your current studies have shaped your interests and how JSI will help you prepare for future graduate education.

Students from non-policy majors should clearly explain how their academic knowledge can contribute to public policy or international affairs.

4. Prepare a Strong Personal Statement

A strong personal statement should address:

  • Your academic and professional interests.
  • The public issues you care about.
  • Your relevant experiences.
  • Your commitment to public service.
  • Your interest in graduate study.
  • Why PPIA is important to your future plans.
  • What perspectives and experiences you would bring to the cohort.

Applicants should avoid simply listing achievements. Instead, they should explain the meaning of their experiences and the impact they hope to make.

5. Choose Recommenders Carefully

Recommendation letters should ideally come from individuals who know the applicant’s academic ability, leadership, work ethic, analytical skills, community involvement, or commitment to public service.

Potential recommenders may include:

  • Professors.
  • Academic advisers.
  • Internship supervisors.
  • Employers.
  • Community leaders.
  • Research supervisors.
  • Leaders of relevant organizations.

Applicants should contact recommenders early and provide them with sufficient information about the programme and application deadline.

6. Review Host-Institution Requirements

Because requirements may differ among Harvard, Princeton, and the University of Michigan, applicants should carefully review the details of their preferred institute.

Pay particular attention to:

  • Academic standing.
  • Citizenship or residency rules.
  • Required coursework.
  • Financial support.
  • Programme dates.
  • Application documents.
  • Graduate school expectations.
  • Travel and housing arrangements.

Click HERE to sign up for live, virtual application seminars to explore the Junior Summer Institute, get practical tips, and ask your questions.

Important Considerations for International Applicants

The PPIA Junior Summer Institute is hosted at U.S. universities, and eligibility for international students may vary by participating institution.

International students should:

  • Confirm whether their preferred JSI school accepts international applicants.
  • Verify that they are enrolled at an eligible accredited U.S. institution, where required.
  • Review citizenship and residency conditions.
  • Confirm whether they can obtain the necessary visa or authorization to participate.
  • Check whether travel support applies to their situation.
  • Review the institution’s specific application instructions.

International applicants should not assume that the general PPIA programme description overrides the eligibility rules of an individual host institution.

Is This a Scholarship, Fellowship, or Internship?

The PPIA Junior Summer Institute is best described as a fully funded fellowship or summer institute rather than a conventional internship or degree scholarship.

It provides:

  • Academic training.
  • Graduate school preparation.
  • Professional development.
  • Financial support.
  • Career guidance.
  • Networking.
  • Access to a public service community.

Participants do not receive a degree from completing JSI. Instead, the programme prepares them for future graduate study and careers in public policy, international affairs, public administration, and related areas.

Why the PPIA Junior Summer Institute Matters

Public policy and international affairs require professionals who can understand complex problems, evaluate evidence, communicate clearly, and work across institutions and communities.

The PPIA Junior Summer Institute helps address this need by supporting undergraduate students before they enter graduate school or professional careers.

The programme gives participants the opportunity to:

  • Experience graduate-level learning.
  • Strengthen quantitative and analytical skills.
  • Understand policy processes.
  • Explore public service careers.
  • Build confidence in academic and professional settings.
  • Connect with peers and mentors.
  • Develop a clearer graduate school plan.
  • Join a community committed to public leadership.

For students who have the ambition to influence public policy or contribute to social change, the programme can serve as an important bridge between undergraduate education, graduate study, and professional service.

Conclusion

The PPIA Junior Summer Institute 2027 offers a fully funded summer experience for undergraduate students interested in public policy, international affairs, public administration, and public service careers.

Selected Fellows will study at Harvard University, Princeton University, or the University of Michigan, where they will participate in graduate-level coursework, develop policy and analytical skills, receive financial support, explore graduate school pathways, and build relationships with peers, faculty, and public service professionals.

The programme may provide tuition, housing, course materials, a summer stipend, travel assistance, career coaching, and other benefits depending on the host institution. Participants may also gain access to graduate school application support, fee waivers, and scholarship opportunities through PPIA’s broader network.

The programme is primarily intended for undergraduate juniors who will have remaining coursework after the summer institute and who demonstrate an interest in public service and future graduate study. Students from a wide range of academic majors may apply, but eligibility requirements—including academic standing, coursework, citizenship, and residency conditions—can vary by host institution.

The application deadline is November 6, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time.

Eligible students should review the official requirements, prepare their application materials early, and submit their applications through the official PPIA application portal before the deadline.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the 2027 With Honor Institute Congressional Fellowship Program, a paid professional fellowship that gives experienced professionals an opportunity to work directly in the United States Congress in Washington, D.C.

Organized by the With Honor Institute (WHI), the program is designed for mid-career professionals interested in public service, Congress, national security, and cross-partisan collaboration. Selected fellows receive intensive congressional training before undertaking a full-time, year-long placement in the personal office of a participating member of the U.S. House of Representatives or U.S. Senate.

The fellowship provides participants with direct exposure to the legislative process while allowing them to contribute their existing professional expertise to congressional work. Military experience is welcomed but is not required for the 2027 program.

About the With Honor Institute

The With Honor Institute is a nonpartisan 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization based in Washington, D.C. Its stated mission focuses on addressing political polarization and supporting more effective cross-partisan cooperation. The organization works with veterans and other servant leaders and emphasizes integrity, civility, and courage.

Its activities include public education, research and nonpartisan analysis, convening leaders from different sectors, and placing mid-career professionals in congressional offices through its Congressional Fellowship Program.

About the 2027 With Honor Institute Congressional Fellowship

The Congressional Fellowship is a 13-month paid professional development and public-service program.

The fellowship begins with intensive congressional training in Washington, D.C. After completing the training component, fellows move into full-time placements with participating congressional offices for approximately one year.

The program is structured to give experienced professionals substantive exposure to the operations of Congress rather than simply providing an observational experience. Fellows become part of the congressional workplace and gain practical experience with the legislative process while contributing their professional knowledge to the offices where they are placed.

WHI describes the program as a mechanism for strengthening congressional office capacity while promoting cooperation across partisan lines through experienced, values-driven professionals.

What Will Fellows Do?

Selected fellows are placed in the personal offices of participating Members of Congress. The fellowship therefore provides participants with an opportunity to understand congressional operations from inside the legislative branch.

Depending on the office, assignments, professional background and needs of the congressional team, the experience may involve areas associated with legislative and congressional work.

The core value of the fellowship is the opportunity to combine a fellow’s previous professional expertise with practical congressional experience.

For professionals who have spent several years developing expertise outside Congress, the program provides a structured route into public service and legislative work.

Fellowship Duration

The 2027 Congressional Fellowship is described as a 13-month paid fellowship.

The structure consists broadly of two components:

  1. Intensive congressional training in Washington, D.C.
  2. A full-time, year-long placement in a participating U.S. House or Senate office.

This distinguishes the opportunity from shorter internships or academic fellowships. Participants should be prepared to make a substantial professional commitment to the program and to work full-time in Washington, D.C.

Who Is the Fellowship Designed For?

The fellowship primarily targets mid-career professionals.

For the 2027 intake, With Honor states that competitive candidates will generally bring approximately five years of professional experience.

The program is particularly relevant to professionals interested in areas such as:

  • Congress and the legislative process
  • Public service
  • National security
  • Public policy
  • Government
  • Cross-partisan cooperation
  • Democratic institutions
  • Leadership and public affairs

The official fellowship page specifically describes the program as being for mid-career professionals interested in Congress and national security.

Military Experience Is Not Required

Although With Honor Institute has a strong organizational focus on veterans and servant leadership, applicants should note an important point about the 2027 fellowship:

Military experience is welcomed, but it is not required.

This means qualified professionals without military backgrounds may also be considered.

The emphasis for the 2027 intake is on finding experienced, values-driven professionals capable of contributing meaningfully to public service and working constructively across political and ideological differences.

Professional Experience

Competitive applicants are expected to have around five years of professional experience.

This requirement reflects the mid-career nature of the program. Unlike many congressional internships intended primarily for university students or recent graduates, this fellowship seeks professionals who can bring established skills, professional judgment and practical experience into a congressional office.

Candidates from different professional sectors may therefore find the fellowship relevant, particularly where their experience can translate effectively into legislative or public-service work.

Skills Sought in Applicants

With Honor indicates that competitive applicants for the 2027 program should demonstrate several important professional attributes, including:

  • Strong written communication skills
  • Strong verbal communication skills
  • Sound professional judgment
  • Approximately five years of professional experience
  • Ability to work effectively with people who hold different ideological perspectives
  • Commitment to public service
  • Interest in bipartisan or cross-partisan collaboration

The ability to work across differences is particularly important because cross-partisan cooperation is central to the Institute’s stated mission.

Why the Fellowship Is Professionally Significant

Working inside a congressional office can provide participants with practical exposure to how federal policymaking operates.

Rather than studying Congress solely from an academic or external professional perspective, fellows work within congressional offices and encounter the legislative environment directly.

The program can therefore help participants develop deeper knowledge of:

  • Congressional processes and institutions
  • Legislative work
  • Policymaking
  • Public-service leadership
  • Congressional office operations
  • Political and ideological differences within policymaking
  • Professional communication in a legislative environment
  • Cross-partisan collaboration

WHI states that fellows gain substantive experience in the legislative process while contributing their existing professional expertise to Congress.

Full-Time Congressional Placement

Following the initial training period, fellows undertake a full-time placement lasting approximately one year.

Placements may be with participating offices in either chamber of Congress:

U.S. House of Representatives

or

U.S. Senate.

The program therefore offers direct institutional exposure to the federal legislative branch.

The exact responsibilities of an individual fellow can depend on the congressional office and its needs.

Training Component

Before entering their congressional placements, selected participants undertake intensive training in Washington, D.C.

This component is particularly valuable for professionals who possess significant expertise in another field but have not previously worked on Capitol Hill.

Training helps participants transition from their existing professional environment into the highly specialized working environment of Congress.

A Program for Experienced Professionals

One of the most distinctive characteristics of the With Honor Institute Congressional Fellowship is its focus on people who already possess substantial professional experience.

Many public-service programs target students or individuals at the beginning of their careers. By contrast, WHI seeks mid-career candidates capable of transferring established expertise into congressional service.

This creates an opportunity for professionals considering a transition toward government, legislative affairs, national security, public policy or broader public service.

Cross-Partisan Collaboration

Cross-partisan cooperation is an important component of the fellowship.

WHI states that its broader mission is to help create a more effective and less polarized Congress. The organization seeks to bridge divides and encourage collaboration among leaders with different political perspectives.

Consequently, applicants should be comfortable operating in an environment where effective professional relationships may require cooperation with people whose political or ideological perspectives differ from their own.

For the 2027 fellowship, With Honor specifically identifies a demonstrated ability to work effectively across ideological differences as a characteristic of competitive applicants.

Location

The fellowship is based in:

Washington, D.C., United States

Because the program involves intensive training followed by a full-time placement in a congressional office, applicants should consider the practical implications of participating in an extended Washington-based professional program.

Is the With Honor Congressional Fellowship Paid?

Yes. With Honor Institute describes its Congressional Fellowship Program as a paid fellowship.

For context, information published for the preceding 2026 fellowship advertised an annual salary of $80,000.

However, applicants should not assume that the same $80,000 figure automatically applies to the 2027 cohort unless it is confirmed in the current 2027 application materials. The current public information retrieved confirms that the 2027 fellowship is paid, but does not provide a verified 2027 compensation figure.

Application Deadline for the 2027 Fellowship

Applications for the 2027 Fellowship are now open. With Honor’s current public update confirms the opening of the 2027 application cycle.

At the time of verification, however, I could not establish a reliable 2027 application deadline from the official fellowship information available through the supplied link.

Applicants should therefore check the current application portal carefully rather than relying on a deadline from an earlier cohort.

For comparison only, the previous application cycle closed on October 1; that date should not be treated as the confirmed deadline for the 2027 intake.

How to Apply

Prospective applicants should use the official With Honor Institute Congressional Fellowship page for current application instructions and the application portal:

Official With Honor Institute Congressional Fellowship Page

Candidates should carefully review the current application materials before submitting, particularly because eligibility requirements, dates, compensation and required documents can change between fellowship cycles.

Given the program’s emphasis on experienced professionals, applicants should be prepared to demonstrate not only their employment history but also how their experience could contribute to congressional work and public service.

What Applicants Should Emphasize

A strong application would logically need to demonstrate alignment with the qualities WHI explicitly identifies for competitive candidates. Applicants should therefore ensure their materials clearly evidence:

  • Relevant professional experience
  • Strong written and oral communication
  • Sound judgment
  • Commitment to public service
  • Ability to operate professionally across ideological differences
  • Interest in Congress and public policy
  • Transferable professional expertise
  • Capacity to contribute effectively within a congressional office

Applicants with military experience may highlight it where relevant, but military service is not a prerequisite for the 2027 fellowship.

Conclusion

The With Honor Institute Congressional Fellowship 2027 offers experienced professionals a distinctive route into federal public service through a paid, 13-month program based in Washington, D.C.

Selected fellows first undertake intensive congressional training and then spend a full year working inside a participating U.S. House or Senate office. The program is particularly suited to mid-career professionals who want practical exposure to Congress, the legislative process, national security or public policy while contributing their existing expertise to congressional work.

Approximately five years of professional experience, strong communication skills, sound judgment and an ability to work constructively across ideological differences are among the qualities identified for competitive applicants. Military experience is welcomed but is not mandatory.

Interested candidates should consult the official fellowship page for the latest application instructions and verify the deadline and 2027-specific terms before submitting.
